athaliah.name: Athaliah
athaliah.charge: Destroying all the seed royal of the house of Judah to reign herself; crying treason when the rightful king was crowned
athaliah.summary: Athaliah of the house of Ahab counselled her son Ahaziah king of Judah in wickedness, and when Jehu killed him she destroyed all the royal seed of Judah to keep the power that had come to her through him (2 Chronicles 22:2-3; 2 Kings 11:1). Jehosheba hid the infant Joash in the house of the Lord six years; in the seventh, Jehoiada the priest crowned him under guard, and when Athaliah tore her clothes and cried treason, she was taken out and killed (2 Kings 11:2-16). Jehoiada renewed the covenant, and the people tore down the house of Baal (2 Kings 11:17-18).
offenseFull: Ahaziah king of Judah was the son of Athaliah, of the house of Omri and Ahab, and he walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, because his mother counselled him in wickedness (2 Chronicles 22:2-3; 2 Kings 8:18, 26). He went to his mother for counsel instead of to the priests and the judges; a woman with a grudge can rule a kingdom through her son. A mama’s boy is not ready to rule, and the Lord does not deal with men who follow behind a woman into sin. When Jehu killed Ahaziah and Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she rose and destroyed all the royal seed (2 Kings 11:1). A mother gave orders to kill anyone next in line, because her power came through her son and she meant to keep it; to stay in power, such women will destroy the men. She did not do it alone; she had weak men helping her run over everything. The teaching reads her as the Jezebel of Thyatira, with the children who follow her (Revelation 2:20-23).

But Jehosheba, daughter of king Joram and wife of Jehoiada the priest, took Joash the son of Ahaziah from among the king’s sons who were being murdered, and hid him and his nurse in a bedroom, and he stayed hidden with her in the house of the Lord six years while Athaliah reigned over the land (2 Kings 11:2-3; 2 Chronicles 22:11-12). The rightful king was kept hidden the whole time the usurper sat on the throne. Her sons, meanwhile, broke up the house of God and gave its dedicated things to the Baals (2 Chronicles 24:7).
judgmentFull: In the seventh year Jehoiada brought the captains of hundreds and the guard into the house of the Lord, made a covenant with them, showed them the king’s son, and set armed men around him on every side with King David’s spears and shields, with orders to kill anyone who came within the ranks (2 Kings 11:4-11). That was order and strategy. He brought out the king’s son, put the crown on him, gave him the testimony, and anointed him, and the people clapped and cried, God save the king (2 Kings 11:12). The saying comes from our forefathers, not from Europe: the priest had to establish a king against a wicked woman who had interfered with the rulership of men.

Athaliah heard the noise and came into the house of the Lord, saw the king standing by the pillar as the custom was, with the trumpeters and all the people rejoicing, and tore her clothes and cried, Treason, treason (2 Kings 11:13-14). She had just killed all the royal seed, and when the rightful king was anointed she screamed treason. When someone tries to restore order, that is how some look at it, as treason against them; they do not see that they are out of order. Jehoiada ordered her taken out between the ranks, and anyone who followed her killed with the sword, because she was not to be slain in the house of the Lord; they seized her, and at the horse entrance to the king’s house she was killed (2 Kings 11:15-16). Twice in the history, when wicked women rose up in power to devour, Jezebel and Athaliah, God sent men of the Lord to remove them for not listening to Him.

Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king and the people, that they should be the Lord’s people; the people tore down the house of Baal, smashed its altars and images, and killed Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars, and the city was quiet (2 Kings 11:17-20). This same covenant is what happens today: as a person repents, keeps the commandments and comes out of idolatry, they become the Lord’s people again. The weapons then were physical; today Israel’s weapon is the scriptures.

Civil leaders and authorities are to be men not women.

Rebellion and insurrection against the government is punishable by death.
You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.

text.text: Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Athaliah the daughter of Omri.
He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab: for his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly.
And when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal.

But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king’s sons which were slain; and they hid him, even him and his nurse, in the bedchamber from Athaliah, so that he was not slain.
And he was with her hid in the house of the Lord six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land.

And the seventh year Jehoiada sent and fetched the rulers over hundreds, with the captains and the guard, and brought them to him into the house of the Lord, and made a covenant with them, and took an oath of them in the house of the Lord, and shewed them the king’s son.
And he commanded them, saying, This is the thing that ye shall do; A third part of you that enter in on the sabbath shall even be keepers of the watch of the king’s house;

baasha.name: Baasha
baasha.charge: Walking in the way of Jeroboam after being exalted out of the dust to destroy Jeroboam’s house
baasha.summary: Baasha conspired against Nadab the son of Jeroboam, killed him, and destroyed all the house of Jeroboam as Ahijah had foretold, then reigned twenty-four years walking in the same way of Jeroboam (1 Kings 15:27-34). He built Ramah to stop the people of the north from going over to Asa and the Lord (2 Chronicles 16:1). The word came by Jehu the son of Hanani that the Lord, who had lifted him out of the dust, would make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and it was fulfilled when Zimri killed his son Elah and all his kin (1 Kings 16:1-13).
offenseFull: Nadab the son of Jeroboam reigned two years and did evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, reigned in his place, and struck all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word the Lord spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite, because of the sins by which Jeroboam made Israel to sin (1 Kings 15:25-30). The study notes mark it as the fulfilment, years later, of the judgment on Jeroboam’s descendants. Then he reigned twenty-four years in Tirzah and did evil in the sight of the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he made Israel commit (1 Kings 15:33-34). The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

He also made war on Judah. There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days, and Baasha came up and built Ramah to keep anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah (1 Kings 15:16-17). The study notes on Chronicles give the reason: tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa, and Baasha was trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah (2 Chronicles 16:1). Asa, instead of crying to the Most High as he had against Zerah, hired Benhadad of Syria with the treasures of the Lord’s house to break his league with Baasha; Benhadad struck the cities of Israel, and Baasha left off building Ramah (2 Chronicles 16:2-6).
judgmentFull: The word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha: the Lord had exalted him out of the dust and made him prince over His people Israel, and he had walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin, provoking Him with their sins. Therefore He would take away the posterity of Baasha and make his house like the house of Jeroboam; the dogs would eat those of his who died in the city, and the birds those who died in the field (1 Kings 16:1-4). The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought. The word came against him both for all the evil he did in walking like Jeroboam and because he killed him (1 Kings 16:7). Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned (1 Kings 16:6).

Elah reigned two years. His servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, killed him while he was drunk in a steward’s house, and as soon as Zimri sat on the throne he killed all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, nor his kinsfolk nor his friends, according to the word spoken by Jehu (1 Kings 16:8-12). It all came for the sins of Baasha and of Elah his son, who provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities (1 Kings 16:13). Moses saw it in the spirit: Israel grew fat and kicked, forsook the God who made him, and provoked Him to jealousy with strange gods (Deuteronomy 32:15-21). A generation later the same sentence was pronounced on Ahab, that his house would be made like the house of Jeroboam and like the house of Baasha (1 Kings 21:22).

text.text: And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.
Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he reigned, that he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.
And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;
Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the Lord against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the Lord, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.
In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years.
And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.

Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben–hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
And Ben–hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel–maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.

But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.
They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.
They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.
Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.
And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.
And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.

They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.

And will make thine house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah, for the provocation wherewith thou hast provoked me to anger, and made Israel to sin.

Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;
Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the Lord against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the Lord, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.
And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.
They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.

belshazzar.name: Belshazzar
belshazzar.charge: Drinking wine from the gold and silver vessels taken out of the temple of the house of God at Jerusalem, with his princes, his wives, and his concubines, and praising the gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone; lifting himself up against the Lord of heaven, having known how his father was humbled
belshazzar.summary: At a feast for a thousand lords, Belshazzar had the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple at Jerusalem brought in, and he, his princes, his wives, and his concubines drank from them and praised gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). A hand wrote on the wall, and Daniel read it: God had counted out his kingdom and ended it, he was weighed and found lacking, and his kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians (Daniel 5:5-28). That same night Belshazzar was slain, and Darius the Mede took the kingdom (Daniel 5:30-31).
offenseFull: Belshazzar the king, not Belteshazzar, which is Daniel, made a great feast, and while tasting the wine commanded that the vessels of the temple be brought so that his lords, wives, and concubines might drink from them, and they praised gods of gold, silver, brass, iron, wood, and stone (Daniel 5:1-4). The study note recalls that even before the captivity Israel was warned it would see these gods of silver and gold in Babylon and was told not to fear or worship them (Baruch 6:3-6). The class says they were mocking the vessels stolen from the temple of the Lord. The text calls Nebuchadnezzar his father; the classes teach that Belshazzar was a later descendant, the margin reading father as grandfather, and one class names him the son of Nabonidus, the king then reigning.

Daniel set his sin before him. The Most High had given Nebuchadnezzar his kingdom and majesty, so that he slew whom he would and set up whom he would, the same power, the teaching says, that America has; but when his heart was lifted up in pride he was put down from his throne and driven out until he knew that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men (Daniel 5:18-21). Belshazzar knew all this and did not humble his heart, but lifted himself against the Lord of heaven, drank from His vessels, and praised gods that neither see nor hear, and did not glorify the God who holds his breath in His hand (Daniel 5:22-23). The teaching puts it to him plainly: you knew about your father being driven out of his kingdom and losing his mind, and you still chose to be arrogant. The study note adds that gods of silver and gold cannot even save themselves (Baruch 6:12-16).
judgmentFull: In the same hour the fingers of a man’s hand wrote on the plaster of the palace wall, and the king’s face changed, his joints were loosed, and his knees knocked together (Daniel 5:5-6). The study note pictures him sitting back with his lords, wives, and concubines having a good time when a hand starts writing on the wall, and he is terrified out of everything. None of his wise men could read it, and he offered scarlet, a chain of gold, and the third place in the kingdom (Daniel 5:7-9); the class explains the third place, since Nabonidus ruled first and Belshazzar second as co-regent. The queen told him of Daniel, in whom was the spirit of the holy gods (Daniel 5:10-12), which the class identifies as the Holy Spirit, the spirit of truth given to those who keep the commandments (John 14:15-17). Daniel, old now after the seventy years in Babylon, told him to keep his gifts (Daniel 5:13-17).

Daniel read the writing: God had counted out the days of the kingdom and ended it; the king was weighed and found lacking; his kingdom was divided and given to the Medes and Persians (Daniel 5:24-28). The class reads it as the end of Babylon’s seventy years: your time is up. Belshazzar clothed Daniel in scarlet and proclaimed him third ruler, and that night Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans was slain, and Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about sixty-two years old (Daniel 5:29-31). The study note marks that the kingdom passed to the Medes and Persians immediately after the interpretation. The teaching says it was an inside job, for the Medes had long been allied with Babylon and lived among them, so Babylon was taken rather than burned; the Babylon prophesied to burn is the one still to come, the one we live in now.

taught.title: Daniel 5: The Handwriting on the Wall

lawsResolved.text: You shall not engage in idolatry and worship or serve the gods, idols or graven images of other nations.
It is vanity and foolish to make and worship idols or graven images.
Pride and arrogance brings decline, punishment and destruction.
Addiction to intoxicating drink brings sorrow, contentions, complaints, wounds without cause, and redness of eyes.

text.text: Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords, and drank wine before the thousand.

Belshazzar, whiles he tasted the wine, commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem; that the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, might drink therein.
Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the temple of the house of God which was at Jerusalem; and the king, and his princes, his wives, and his concubines, drank in them.
They drank wine, and praised the gods of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of stone.
In the same hour came forth fingers of a man’s hand, and wrote over against the candlestick upon the plaister of the wall of the king’s palace: and the king saw the part of the hand that wrote.
Then the king’s countenance was changed, and his thoughts troubled him, so that the joints of his loins were loosed, and his knees smote one against another.

The king cried aloud to bring in the astrologers, the Chaldeans, and the soothsayers. And the king spake, and said to the wise men of Babylon, Whosoever shall read this writing, and shew me the interpretation thereof, shall be clothed with scarlet, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Then came in all the king’s wise men: but they could not read the writing, nor make known to the king the interpretation thereof.
Then was king Belshazzar greatly troubled, and his countenance was changed in him, and his lords were astonied.

Now the queen, by reason of the words of the king and his lords, came into the banquet house: and the queen spake and said, O king, live for ever: let not thy thoughts trouble thee, nor let thy countenance be changed:

There is a man in thy kingdom, in whom is the spirit of the holy gods; and in the days of thy father light and understanding and wisdom, like the wisdom of the gods, was found in him; whom the king Nebuchadnezzar thy father, the king, I say, thy father, made master of the magicians, astrologers, Chaldeans, and soothsayers;

Forasmuch as an excellent spirit, and knowledge, and understanding, interpreting of dreams, and shewing of hard sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar: now let Daniel be called, and he will shew the interpretation.

Then was Daniel brought in before the king. And the king spake and said unto Daniel, Art thou that Daniel, which art of the children of the captivity of Judah, whom the king my father brought out of Jewry?
I have even heard of thee, that the spirit of the gods is in thee, and that light and understanding and excellent wisdom is found in thee.

And now the wise men, the astrologers, have been brought in before me, that they should read this writing, and make known unto me the interpretation thereof: but they could not shew the interpretation of the thing:

And I have heard of thee, that thou canst make interpretations, and dissolve doubts: now if thou canst read the writing, and make known to me the interpretation thereof, thou shalt be clothed with scarlet, and have a chain of gold about thy neck, and shalt be the third ruler in the kingdom.
Then Daniel answered and said before the king, Let thy gifts be to thyself, and give thy rewards to another; yet I will read the writing unto the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
O thou king, the most high God gave Nebuchadnezzar thy father a kingdom, and majesty, and glory, and honour:

And for the majesty that he gave him, all people, nations, and languages, trembled and feared before him: whom he would he slew; and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he set up; and whom he would he put down.
But when his heart was lifted up, and his mind hardened in pride, he was deposed from his kingly throne, and they took his glory from him:

And he was driven from the sons of men; and his heart was made like the beasts, and his dwelling was with the wild asses: they fed him with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of heaven; till he knew that the most high God ruled in the kingdom of men, and that he appointeth over it whomsoever he will.
And thou his son, O Belshazzar, hast not humbled thine heart, though thou knewest all this;

But hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven; and they have brought the vessels of his house before thee, and thou, and thy lords, thy wives, and thy concubines, have drunk wine in them; and thou hast praised the gods of silver, and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and stone, which see not, nor hear, nor know: and the God in whose hand thy breath is, and whose are all thy ways, hast thou not glorified:
Then was the part of the hand sent from him; and this writing was written.
And this is the writing that was written, MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; God hath numbered thy kingdom, and finished it.
TEKEL; Thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
PERES; Thy kingdom is divided, and given to the Medes and Persians.

And Darius the Median took the kingdom, being about threescore and two years old.
So when ye be come unto Babylon, ye shall remain there many years, and for a long season, namely, seven generations: and after that I will bring you away peaceably from thence.
Now shall ye see in Babylon gods of silver, and of gold, and of wood, borne upon shoulders, which cause the nations to fear.
Beware therefore that ye in no wise be like to strangers, neither be ye afraid of them, when ye see the multitude before them and behind them, worshipping them.
But say ye in your hearts, O Lord, we must worship thee.

Yet cannot these gods save themselves from rust and moth, though they be covered with purple raiment.
They wipe their faces because of the dust of the temple, when there is much upon them.
And he that cannot put to death one that offendeth him holdeth a sceptre, as though he were a judge of the country.
He hath also in his right hand a dagger and an axe: but cannot deliver himself from war and thieves.

cain.name: Cain
cain.charge: Bringing of the fruit of the ground when the sacrificial law required a firstling; refusing correction; and murder of his brother Abel
cain.summary: Cain was the firstborn of the house after it was put out of the garden, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field. He knew the sacrifice ordained in the garden and in process of time brought fruit of the ground instead. Corrected, he grew bitter; called to repent, he refused. He talked with his brother as a friend, drew him out to the field and killed him, then lied to God’s face and took no accountability. Cursed from the earth, marked, and made a fugitive and a vagabond, he built a city in the east among the people already on the earth, and his line carried the music and the weapons until the earth was filled with violence.
offenseFull: Cain was born first, a tiller of the ground and a man of the field, and the ground had been cursed in chapter three, so it did not yield easily (Genesis 4:1-3; Genesis 3:17). He knew the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained when Adam was clothed with skins (Genesis 3:21; Genesis 9:5). In process of time he brought fruit of the ground; the words in process of time say the falling off was gradual, not sudden. The Lord had no respect to it, and Cain was very wroth and his countenance fell (Genesis 4:3-5). What started it was correction. Correction is grievous to the man who leaves the way, and only by pride comes contention; that grievous spirit nourished envy into bitterness, and Cain is the first hater the scriptures record (Proverbs 15:10; Proverbs 13:10).

The Most High called him to repent: if he did well he would be accepted, and if not, sin lay at the door, and the door is his own mind, and the desire of that sin would be toward him and it would rule over him (Genesis 4:7). Cain talked with his brother, playing the friend while Abel, a prophet, urged him to repent, and drew him out to the field where he spent his days, and killed him there (Genesis 4:8). Christ named the line when he told the men who were plotting his death that they were of their father the devil, a murderer from the beginning, who did not abide in the truth, a liar and the father of it: Satan murdered nobody in the beginning, Cain did, and Cain lied (John 8:44). John says the same, that he was of that wicked one, and killed

his brother because his own works were evil and his brother’s righteous (1 John 3:12). Where envying and strife are, there is confusion and every evil work, and confusion is where every evil work hides (James 3:16). Asked where his brother was, he answered with a lie and a taunt and took no accountability at all (Genesis 4:9).
judgmentFull: Abel’s blood cried from the ground. Cain was cursed from the earth, the ground would no longer yield him her strength, and he was made a fugitive and a vagabond: the same low estate spoken to the serpent (Genesis 4:10-12; Genesis 3:14). A fugitive is a man who kills and escapes the sentence; a vagabond wanders from land to land and settles nowhere that belongs to him, and wherever he goes the ground does not answer him. The curse reached the man himself. Adam was formed of the ground, and the ground was cursed for Cain; the mark set upon him changed him, for at the beginning he looked like everybody else, and his own fear that anyone finding him would kill him says both that the earth was already peopled and that he now stood out among them (Genesis 4:14-15). Vengeance sevenfold was threatened against his killer, and the Most High reserved the matter to himself. From the face of God he would be hid: the Most High stopped dealing with him, and the father he had left was the wicked one.

He went out from the presence of the Lord and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden, the same ground where the cherubims and the flaming sword were set; he found a wife among the people already there and built a city, which is not built for three people, and called it after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names (Genesis 4:16-17; Psalms 49:11). The older scholars of Assyria identified that city with Unug, which the Akkadians called Uruk and which scripture calls Erech, and Nimrod later built the beginning of his kingdom on the same ground in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10:8-10). His line kept the trades. Jubal fathered all such as handle the harp and the organ, and music in the wrong hands is a weapon; Tubalcain instructed every craftsman in brass and iron, which is the making of arms, and the Most High says he created the smith that blows the coals and created the waster to destroy (Genesis 4:20-22; Isaiah 54:16). Wisdom says the unrighteous man who went away from her in his anger perished in the same fury with which he murdered his brother, and names his cause as the cause for which the earth was drowned (Wisdom of Solomon 10:3-4; Genesis 6:1-2). The way of Cain stands condemned (Jude 1:11), and the same spirit appears again in Esau, the firstborn, the man of the field, who purposed in his heart to kill his brother (Genesis 27:41).

text.text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the Lord.
And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.

And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
And surely your blood of your lives will I require; at the hand of every beast will I require it, and at the hand of man; at the hand of every man’s brother will I require the life of man.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.
Only by pride cometh contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen?
If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.
And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.
And the Lord said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?
And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.

Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.
For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.

And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:
And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;
When thou tillest the ground, it shall not henceforth yield unto thee her strength; a fugitive and a vagabond shalt thou be in the earth.
And Cain said unto the Lord, My punishment is greater than I can bear.

Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid; and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me.
And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.
And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.
And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.
Their inward thought is, that their houses shall continue for ever, and their dwelling places to all generations; they call their lands after their own names.
And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.
He was a mighty hunter before the Lord: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the Lord.
And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.
And Adah bare Jabal: he was the father of such as dwell in tents, and of such as have cattle.
And his brother’s name was Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.
And Zillah, she also bare Tubal–cain, an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron: and the sister of Tubal–cain was Naamah.
Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.
But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.
For whose cause the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it, and directed the course of the righteous in a piece of wood of small value.
And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them,
That the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.
Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.

daniel.name: Daniel
daniel.charge: Purposing in his heart not to defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat nor with the wine which he drank; kneeling and praying three times a day with his windows open toward Jerusalem, as he did aforetime, after the decree was signed
daniel.summary: Daniel, of the king’s seed of Judah, was carried to Babylon with the best of Israel’s youth to be trained for the king’s service, and he resolved not to defile himself with the king’s meat and wine; God gave him favour, and he and his companions were found ten times wiser than all the king’s wise men (Daniel 1:1-20). Under Darius, when his rivals could find no fault in him except concerning the law of his God, he kept praying three times a day toward Jerusalem after the decree was signed, and God shut the lions’ mouths (Daniel 6:1-23). He prospered under Darius and Cyrus and was told he would stand in his lot at the end of the days (Daniel 6:28; Daniel 12:13).
offenseFull: When Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem he carried off vessels of the house of God, as the prophets had warned, and Isaiah had told Hezekiah that his sons would be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon (Daniel 1:1-2; 2 Kings 20:16-18). The king had the master of his eunuchs bring children of the king’s seed and the princes, without blemish and skilled in wisdom, to be taught the tongue of the Chaldeans and fed from the king’s table (Daniel 1:3-5). The class teaches that Babylon did not take any old body; they took the best and most educated to build up their kingdom, and Esau did the same when he took the best of our people and put them in North America. The study note adds that our people still serve in governments and are used to build a system that is not their own, often assimilated and well rewarded for it. The prince of the eunuchs renamed Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah as Belteshazzar, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego (Daniel 1:6-7), part of the assimilation; the study notes compare it to Hadassah made Esther, and the teaching to our fathers in slavery whose names were changed.

But Daniel resolved in his heart not to defile himself with the king’s meat or his wine, and asked the prince of the eunuchs to spare him (Daniel 1:8). God brought him into favour, for the Lord causes the enemy to treat His remnant well in the time of evil (Jeremiah 15:11). The officer feared for his head if they looked worse than the others, so Daniel asked for a ten day proof on pulse, which the teaching explains as vegetables, the green herb given for meat in the beginning (Genesis 1:29), and water; at the end they looked fairer and fuller than all who ate the king’s meat (Daniel 1:9-16).

Under Darius, Daniel was first of three presidents over a hundred and twenty princes, preferred because an excellent spirit was in him, and when the others sought occasion against him they found no error or fault (Daniel 6:1-4). The study note says this is how our forefathers rolled, keeping a clear conscience before God and men (Acts 24:16), and the class says he lived up to a name, integrity. They could find nothing against him except concerning the law of his God, so they had Darius sign a decree that no one petition any god or man but the king for thirty days (Daniel 6:5-9). When Daniel knew it was signed he went home, and with his windows open toward Jerusalem he knelt three times a day and prayed and gave thanks, as he had done before (Daniel 6:10).
judgmentFull: God gave the four children knowledge and skill in all learning, and Daniel understanding in all visions and dreams; the king found them ten times better than all his magicians and astrologers (Daniel 1:17-20). The verse by verse teaching says the Most High gave them that understanding and they could not be outdone, as with Moses before the magicians, and points to Susanna, where young Daniel exposed the lying elders (Susanna 1:45-62). He continued to the first year of Cyrus (Daniel 1:21).

Cast into the den, he told the king that God had sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths, because he was found innocent, and he came up unharmed because he trusted in his God (Daniel 6:16-23). The study note joins to this the account of Habakkuk carried by an angel with food for Daniel in the den, for God does not forsake those who seek and love Him (Bel and the Dragon 1:33-39). His accusers went into the den in his place (Daniel 6:24), for when a man’s ways please the Lord He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him (Proverbs 16:7). Darius commanded all his dominion to tremble before the God of Daniel, and Daniel prospered under Darius and Cyrus the Persian (Daniel 6:25-28); a reference work read in class calls him one of the few well known men of the Bible of whom nothing negative is written.

Daniel was told that he would rest, and at the end of the days stand in his lot (Daniel 12:13). The study note reads rest as his death and the promise as the Most High sending these leaders back to us, and the verse by verse class teaches that Daniel is on the earth in the time of the end, raising up his people and understanding what was sealed from him, though no one knows who he is.

text.text: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon unto Jerusalem, and besieged it.

And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with part of the vessels of the house of God: which he carried into the land of Shinar to the house of his god; and he brought the vessels into the treasure house of his god.
And the king spake unto Ashpenaz the master of his eunuchs, that he should bring certain of the children of Israel, and of the king’s seed, and of the princes;

Children in whom was no blemish, but well favoured, and skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science, and such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace, and whom they might teach the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans.
And the king appointed them a daily provision of the king’s meat, and of the wine which he drank: so nourishing them three years, that at the end thereof they might stand before the king.
Now among these were of the children of Judah, Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
Unto whom the prince of the eunuchs gave names: for he gave unto Daniel the name of Belteshazzar; and to Hananiah, of Shadrach; and to Mishael, of Meshach; and to Azariah, of Abed–nego.

But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Now God had brought Daniel into favour and tender love with the prince of the eunuchs.

And the prince of the eunuchs said unto Daniel, I fear my lord the king, who hath appointed your meat and your drink: for why should he see your faces worse liking than the children which are of your sort? then shall ye make me endanger my head to the king.
Then said Daniel to Melzar, whom the prince of the eunuchs had set over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us pulse to eat, and water to drink.
Then let our countenances be looked upon before thee, and the countenance of the children that eat of the portion of the king’s meat: and as thou seest, deal with thy servants.
So he consented to them in this matter, and proved them ten days.
And at the end of ten days their countenances appeared fairer and fatter in flesh than all the children which did eat the portion of the king’s meat.
Thus Melzar took away the portion of their meat, and the wine that they should drink; and gave them pulse.
As for these four children, God gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom: and Daniel had understanding in all visions and dreams.
Now at the end of the days that the king had said he should bring them in, then the prince of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
And the king communed with them; and among them all was found none like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah: therefore stood they before the king.
And in all matters of wisdom and understanding, that the king enquired of them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and astrologers that were in all his realm.
It pleased Darius to set over the kingdom an hundred and twenty princes, which should be over the whole kingdom;
And over these three presidents; of whom Daniel was first: that the princes might give accounts unto them, and the king should have no damage.
Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.

Then the presidents and princes sought to find occasion against Daniel concerning the kingdom; but they could find none occasion nor fault; forasmuch as he was faithful, neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then said these men, We shall not find any occasion against this Daniel, except we find it against him concerning the law of his God.
Then these presidents and princes assembled together to the king, and said thus unto him, King Darius, live for ever.

All the presidents of the kingdom, the governors, and the princes, the counsellors, and the captains, have consulted together to establish a royal statute, and to make a firm decree, that whosoever shall ask a petition of any God or man for thirty days, save of thee, O king, he shall be cast into the den of lions.
Now, O king, establish the decree, and sign the writing, that it be not changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.
Wherefore king Darius signed the writing and the decree.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.
Then these men assembled, and found Daniel praying and making supplication before his God.

Then they came near, and spake before the king concerning the king’s decree; Hast thou not signed a decree, that every man that shall ask a petition of any God or man within thirty days, save of thee, O king, shall be cast into the den of lions? The king answered and said, The thing is true, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which altereth not.

Then answered they and said before the king, That Daniel, which is of the children of the captivity of Judah, regardeth not thee, O king, nor the decree that thou hast signed, but maketh his petition three times a day.
Then the king, when he heard these words, was sore displeased with himself, and set his heart on Daniel to deliver him: and he laboured till the going down of the sun to deliver him.
Then these men assembled unto the king, and said unto the king, Know, O king, that the law of the Medes and Persians is, That no decree nor statute which the king establisheth may be changed.

daniels-accusers.name: Daniel’s accusers
daniels-accusers.charge: Seeking occasion against Daniel and finding none; procuring a decree by the law of the Medes and Persians that no man petition any god or man for thirty days save the king, to take him in the law of his God; assembling to find him praying and pressing the king to cast him to the lions
daniels-accusers.summary: The presidents and princes under Darius sought occasion against Daniel and found no fault in him except concerning the law of his God, so they had the king sign an unchangeable decree that no one petition any god or man but the king for thirty days (Daniel 6:4-9). They found Daniel praying toward Jerusalem as before, reported him, and pressed the king until Daniel was cast to the lions (Daniel 6:10-17). God shut the lions’ mouths, and the king had the accusers, their children, and their wives cast into the den, where the lions broke their bones before they reached the bottom (Daniel 6:22-24).
offenseFull: Darius set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom and three presidents over them, Daniel first, and thought to set him over the whole realm because an excellent spirit was in him (Daniel 6:1-3). The presidents and princes sought occasion against him concerning the kingdom and found none, because he was faithful and no error or fault was in him (Daniel 6:4). The class renders their thinking: we cannot find fault with his work, so we will use his religion against him. The study note says they really hated Daniel and knew the only way to find fault was concerning the law of his God (Daniel 6:5).

They came to the king claiming that all the rulers had agreed, and persuaded him to sign a decree that anyone who asked a petition of any god or man but the king for thirty days be cast into the den of lions, by the law of the Medes and Persians, which does not change (Daniel 6:6-9). The teaching explains that in the Persian empire a decree once sent out could not be reversed, and the king’s counsellors held him to it. They gathered, found Daniel praying and making supplication to his God, reminded the king of his decree, and reported that Daniel, of the captivity of Judah, did not regard him or his decree (Daniel 6:10-13). The king laboured till sundown to deliver him, but they pressed him that no decree of the Medes and Persians could be changed (Daniel 6:14-15). The class reads beside this the account in Bel and the Dragon, where the people of Babylon said the king had become a Jew and threatened to destroy him and his house unless he delivered Daniel to them (Bel and the Dragon 1:28-30). The king, displeased with himself, commanded Daniel cast in, saying that the God he served continually would deliver him, and the den was sealed (Daniel 6:16-17).
judgmentFull: The king passed the night fasting, with no music and no sleep, and hurried to the den at dawn; Daniel answered that God had sent His angel and shut the lions’ mouths, because he was found innocent before God and had done the king no hurt (Daniel 6:18-22). The class sets beside it the Bel and the Dragon account, in which seven lions were kept hungry so they would devour Daniel, the prophet Habakkuk was carried by an angel to feed him in the den, and the king cried that the God of Daniel is great and there is none other (Bel and the Dragon 1:31-41).

Then the king commanded that the men who had accused Daniel be cast into the den, they, their children, and their wives, and the lions overpowered them and broke all their bones before they came to the bottom (Daniel 6:24). The class says the lions that had been held back from Daniel devoured those who set him up. The law of the false witness is to do to him as he thought to do to his brother (Deuteronomy 19:16-19), and the study note on that law says that whoever falsely accuses a man of a crime worthy of death is put to death, because that is what he intended for his neighbour, and that false witnesses arising among our own people were part of why the nation fell into captivity. When a man’s ways please the Lord, He makes even his enemies to be at peace with him (Proverbs 16:7). Darius then wrote to every people that in all his dominion men should tremble before the God of Daniel, the living God whose kingdom shall not be destroyed (Daniel 6:25-27).

lawsResolved.text: Do not join your hand with a wicked man to be an unrighteous witness.
If a witness is found to be a false witness by testifying falsely against his brother, then he shall receive the punishment that the accused brethren would have received if guilty.
Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
Deceit and fraud a characteristic of the wicked.
Punishment is the fruit and reward for iniquity and wicked ways (you shall reap that which you sow).

david.name: David
david.charge: A man after the Lord’s own heart: twice sparing the Lord’s anointed, leaving vengeance with the Lord, and repenting when he fell
david.summary: Samuel named the replacement at Gilgal before he had ever met him: the Lord had sought a man after His own heart and commanded him to be captain over His people. Twice Saul was delivered into David’s hand, in the cave at Engedi and in the trench at Hachilah, and twice David would not stretch out his hand against the Lord’s anointed, leaving the judgment with the Most High. He reverenced the man who was hunting him, and he judged the men who shed blood in his name. When he fell he had godly sorrow and rose again; his one great fall is its own case, and this is the rest.
offenseFull: Samuel told Saul at Gilgal that his kingdom would not continue, because the Lord had sought a man after His own heart and commanded him to be captain over His people (1 Samuel 13:14); the prophet said it without ever having met the replacement, and the apostle repeated the testimony, that the Lord had found in David the son of Jesse a man after His own heart who would fulfil all His will (Acts 13:22). What that heart looks like is shown while Saul hunted him. Saul took three thousand chosen men to the rocks of the wild goats and went into a cave to cover his feet, which is the scripture’s way of saying he was in there relieving himself, and David and his men were staying in the sides of it (1 Samuel 24:2-13). David rose and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily, the corner of a man’s garment where the fringes are attached, and afterward his heart smote him even for that, and he stayed his servants, saying the Lord forbid that he should do such a thing to his master, the Lord’s anointed (1 Samuel 24:4-7). Then he went out after him, called him his lord the king, bowed with his face to the earth, laid the proof in his hand, and left the case with the Most High to judge between them, since his own hand would not touch him. Saul wept and admitted that David was more righteous, having repaid him good for evil, and that he knew well David would surely be king (1 Samuel 24:16-20). A king shall reign in righteousness (Isaiah 32:1); that is what Saul was acknowledging.
It happened again in the wilderness of Ziph. Saul lay sleeping in the trench with his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster and Abner and the people round about him, and Abishai

asked leave to pin him to the earth with one stroke and not need a second. David answered that no man could stretch out his hand against the Lord’s anointed and be guiltless; as the Lord lived, the Lord would smite him, or his day would come to die, or he would go down into battle and perish (1 Samuel 26:7-11). These were warriors and they were itching for it, but David took the bigger position: this man was chosen before me, so let God deal with him. Saul had men around him whispering that David thought himself better and wanted the throne,, and he fed into it instead of saying that David was a man of God. David cried from the hill that if the Lord had stirred Saul up against him, let Him accept an offering, but if it was the children of men, let them be cursed before the Lord, and Saul confessed that he had played the fool and erred exceedingly (1 Samuel 26:19-21). The same spirit met Shimei on the road out of Jerusalem, and David let him curse, saying it might be that the Lord would look on his affliction and repay him good for the cursing that day (2 Samuel 16:10-12).
judgmentFull: The Lord built him a house: his house and his kingdom would be established for ever before Him, and his throne established for ever (2 Samuel 7:16). When a stranger claimed the crown of Saul, and when two captains carried in the head of Ish-bosheth, he did not accept wickedness done in his name; both were put to death for taking a life not ordained of the Lord nor commanded by the king (2 Samuel 1:14-16; 2 Samuel 4:9-12), because all things are to be done decently and in order (1 Corinthians 14:40). When Nathan told him he was the man, he confessed that he had sinned against the Lord (2 Samuel 12:13), and his sorrow was the godly sorrow that works repentance to salvation (2 Corinthians 7:10); a just man falls seven times and rises up again (Proverbs 24:16). Fleeing from Absalom he sent the ark back into the city in faith: if he found favour in the eyes of the Lord, He would bring him again to see it, and if not, let Him do what seemed good (2 Samuel 15:25-26). The Lord took away his sins and exalted his horn for ever, giving him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel (Ecclesiasticus 47:11). The throne stands on the stipulation he gave Solomon at the last, to keep the charge of the Lord his God and walk in His ways and keep His statutes and commandments as written in the law of Moses (1 Kings 2:3-4); and the throne of his father David is the one given to Christ, whose kingdom shall have no end (Luke 1:32-33).

text.text: But now thy kingdom shall not continue: the Lord hath sought him a man after his own heart, and the Lord hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which the Lord commanded thee.

And when he had removed him, he raised up unto them David to be their king; to whom also he gave testimony, and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.
Then Saul took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats.
And he came to the sheepcotes by the way, where was a cave; and Saul went in to cover his feet: and David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.

And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the Lord said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.
And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
And he said unto his men, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord’s anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the Lord.
So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
David also arose afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried after Saul, saying, My lord the king. And when Saul looked behind him, David stooped with his face to the earth, and bowed himself.
And David said to Saul, Wherefore hearest thou men’s words, saying, Behold, David seeketh thy hurt?

Behold, this day thine eyes have seen how that the Lord had delivered thee to day into mine hand in the cave: and some bade me kill thee: but mine eye spared thee; and I said, I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the Lord’s anointed.

Moreover, my father, see, yea, see the skirt of thy robe in my hand: for in that I cut off the skirt of thy robe, and killed thee not, know thou and see that there is neither evil nor transgression in mine hand, and I have not sinned against thee; yet thou huntest my soul to take it.
The Lord judge between me and thee, and the Lord avenge me of thee: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.
As saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.

And the men of David said unto him, Behold the day of which the Lord said unto thee, Behold, I will deliver thine enemy into thine hand, that thou mayest do to him as it shall seem good unto thee. Then David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily.
And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul’s skirt.
And he said unto his men, The Lord forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the Lord’s anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him, seeing he is the anointed of the Lord.
So David stayed his servants with these words, and suffered them not to rise against Saul. But Saul rose up out of the cave, and went on his way.
And it came to pass, when David had made an end of speaking these words unto Saul, that Saul said, Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept.
And he said to David, Thou art more righteous than I: for thou hast rewarded me good, whereas I have rewarded thee evil.
And thou hast shewed this day how that thou hast dealt well with me: forasmuch as when the Lord had delivered me into thine hand, thou killedst me not.
For if a man find his enemy, will he let him go well away? wherefore the Lord reward thee good for that thou hast done unto me this day.
And now, behold, I know well that thou shalt surely be king, and that the kingdom of Israel shall be established in thine hand.
Behold, a king shall reign in righteousness, and princes shall rule in judgment.
So David and Abishai came to the people by night: and, behold, Saul lay sleeping within the trench, and his spear stuck in the ground at his bolster: but Abner and the people lay round about him.

Then said Abishai to David, God hath delivered thine enemy into thine hand this day: now therefore let me smite him, I pray thee, with the spear even to the earth at once, and I will not smite him the second time.
And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord’s anointed, and be guiltless?
David said furthermore, As the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.

Now therefore, I pray thee, let my lord the king hear the words of his servant. If the Lord have stirred thee up against me, let him accept an offering: but if they be the children of men, cursed be they before the Lord; for they have driven me out this day from abiding in the inheritance of the Lord, saying, Go, serve other gods.
Now therefore, let not my blood fall to the earth before the face of the Lord: for the king of Israel is come out to seek a flea, as when one doth hunt a partridge in the mountains.
Then said Saul, I have sinned: return, my son David: for I will no more do thee harm, because my soul was precious in thine eyes this day: behold, I have played the fool, and have erred exceedingly.
And the king said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah? so let him curse, because the Lord hath said unto him, Curse David. Who shall then say, Wherefore hast thou done so?

And David said to Abishai, and to all his servants, Behold, my son, which came forth of my bowels, seeketh my life: how much more now may this Benjamite do it? let him alone, and let him curse; for the Lord hath bidden him.
It may be that the Lord will look on mine affliction, and that the Lord will requite me good for his cursing this day.
And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?
And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the Lord’s anointed.
And David answered Rechab and Baanah his brother, the sons of Rimmon the Beerothite, and said unto them, As the Lord liveth, who hath redeemed my soul out of all adversity,
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:

And David commanded his young men, and they slew them, and cut off their hands and their feet, and hanged them up over the pool in Hebron. But they took the head of Ish–bosheth, and buried it in the sepulchre of Abner in Hebron.
Let all things be done decently and in order.
And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.
And the king said unto Zadok, Carry back the ark of God into the city: if I shall find favour in the eyes of the Lord, he will bring me again, and shew me both it, and his habitation:
But if he thus say, I have no delight in thee; behold, here am I, let him do to me as seemeth good unto him.
The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.

And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself:

That the Lord may continue his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.
He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
And David said to Abishai, Destroy him not: for who can stretch forth his hand against the Lord’s anointed, and be guiltless?
David said furthermore, As the Lord liveth, the Lord shall smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall descend into battle, and perish.
The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.

david-and-bathsheba.name: David and Bathsheba
david-and-bathsheba.charge: Adultery with the wife of Uriah, and setting Uriah up to be murdered on the battlefield to cover it
david-and-bathsheba.summary: In the season when kings went out to war, David stayed behind in Jerusalem, saw a woman bathing from his roof, was told plainly that she was the wife of Uriah the Hittite, and sent for her anyway. When she conceived he called Uriah home to cover it, and when Uriah would not go down to his house he sent him back carrying his own death warrant. Nathan came with a parable, David pronounced sentence on himself, and Nathan told him he was the man. The Lord took away his sin, but the sword never left his house, and the child died.
offenseFull: While Joab and all Israel were sent to destroy the Ammonites and besiege Rabbah, David stayed in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 11:1). Walking on the roof of his house in the evening he saw a woman bathing, asked after her, and was told she was Bath-sheba the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite (2 Samuel 11:2-3). He was told plainly that she was a married woman, and he had known the law from his youth up. He sent for her and lay with her, and she conceived and sent him word that she was pregnant (2 Samuel 11:4-5). Bath-sheba was not innocent either; when the king called she went, and she did not refuse.

David sent for Uriah and told him to go down to his house, with a gift of food following him from the king; but Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with the servants and did not go home (2 Samuel 11:6-9). He answered that the ark and Israel and Judah were living in tents and his lord’s servants were camped in the open field, so how could he go into his own house (2 Samuel 11:11). David made him drunk, and even drunk he would not go down (2 Samuel 11:13). That loyalty was killing David all the more.

In the morning David wrote to Joab and sent the letter by Uriah’s own hand, ordering that he be put at the front of the fiercest fighting and abandoned there to be killed (2 Samuel 11:14-15). Joab placed him where he knew the valiant men were, and Uriah died along with some of David’s servants (2 Samuel 11:16-17); other men of Israel died with that sin. The curses at Ebal are for this: a curse lies on the man who strikes his neighbour in secret and on the man who takes a reward to kill an innocent person, and the reward here was the woman (Deuteronomy 27:24-25). David sent word to Joab not to be troubled, since in battle the sword kills this man or that one (2 Samuel 11:25). When the mourning was over he married her, but the Lord was displeased with what David had done (2 Samuel 11:27).
judgmentFull: The Lord sent Nathan with a parable of a rich man with many flocks who took a poor man’s one ewe lamb, dear to him as a daughter, to feed a traveller. David burned with anger and swore the man deserved to die, because he had no pity (2 Samuel 12:1-5); judging that man, he was pronouncing sentence on himself. Nathan told him he was the man: the Lord had anointed him, delivered him from Saul, given him his master’s house and all Israel and Judah, and would have given him more; why then had he despised the Lord’s commandment, killing Uriah and taking his wife (2 Samuel 12:7-9)? If he had only asked, the Lord would have given him anything.

So the sword would never leave his house; the Lord would raise up trouble from within it and give his wives to another man in broad daylight, because he had acted in secret and this would be done before all Israel (2 Samuel 12:10-12). It came to pass exactly, on a roof, by Ahithophel’s counsel. David confessed his sin against the Lord, and Nathan told him the Lord had taken it away and he would not die, but because the deed had given the Lord’s enemies great cause to blaspheme, the child would die (2 Samuel 12:13-14). That child was the judgment: the Lord shows mercy and forgives iniquity, yet does not clear the guilty (Exodus 34:7). He was pardoned; he was not cleared. He fasted and lay on the ground all night while the child lived; when it died he rose, washed, worshipped and ate, saying he would go to the child but the child would not come back to him (2 Samuel 12:16-23). His was the godly sorrow that leads to repentance (2 Corinthians 7:10); a just man who falls seven times gets up again (Proverbs 24:16). Through the judgment Solomon was still born and the Lord loved him (2 Samuel 12:24-25). People who want to justify wrongdoing run straight to this history; but you are not King David, and this is the mess up, not the licence.

And David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in unto him, and he lay with her; for she was purified from her uncleanness: and she returned unto her house.
And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.
And David sent to Joab, saying, Send me Uriah the Hittite. And Joab sent Uriah to David.
And when Uriah was come unto him, David demanded of him how Joab did, and how the people did, and how the war prospered.
And David said to Uriah, Go down to thy house, and wash thy feet. And Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and there followed him a mess of meat from the king.
But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and went not down to his house.

And Uriah said unto David, The ark, and Israel, and Judah, abide in tents; and my lord Joab, and the servants of my lord, are encamped in the open fields; shall I then go into mine house, to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? as thou livest, and as thy soul liveth, I will not do this thing.
And when David had called him, he did eat and drink before him; and he made him drunk: and at even he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but went not down to his house.
And it came to pass in the morning, that David wrote a letter to Joab, and sent it by the hand of Uriah.
And he wrote in the letter, saying, Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle, and retire ye from him, that he may be smitten, and die.
And it came to pass, when Joab observed the city, that he assigned Uriah unto a place where he knew that valiant men were.
And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.

Then David said unto the messenger, Thus shalt thou say unto Joab, Let not this thing displease thee, for the sword devoureth one as well as another: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it: and encourage thou him.

The rich man had exceeding many flocks and herds:

And there came a traveller unto the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to dress for the wayfaring man that was come unto him; but took the poor man’s lamb, and dressed it for the man that was come to him.
And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the Lord liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
And Nathan said to David, Thou art the man. Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I anointed thee king over Israel, and I delivered thee out of the hand of Saul;

Wherefore hast thou despised the commandment of the Lord, to do evil in his sight? thou hast killed Uriah the Hittite with the sword, and hast taken his wife to be thy wife, and hast slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.
Now therefore the sword shall never depart from thine house; because thou hast despised me, and hast taken the wife of Uriah the Hittite to be thy wife.

Thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house, and I will take thy wives before thine eyes, and give them unto thy neighbour, and he shall lie with thy wives in the sight of this sun.
For thou didst it secretly: but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.
And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the Lord. And Nathan said unto David, The Lord also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.
Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.

Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.
David therefore besought God for the child; and David fasted, and went in, and lay all night upon the earth.
And the elders of his house arose, and went to him, to raise him up from the earth: but he would not, neither did he eat bread with them.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. But when David saw that his servants whispered, David perceived that the child was dead: therefore David said unto his servants, Is the child dead? And they said, He is dead.
