davids-census.name: David’s numbering of the people
davids-census.charge: Numbering Israel and Judah against Joab’s counsel; seventy thousand men dead of the pestilence
davids-census.summary: The anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel, and he moved David to number Israel and Judah; the Chronicles account says Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to do it (2 Samuel 24:1; 1 Chronicles 21:1). The king’s word prevailed over Joab’s objection, and when the count came in David’s conscience struck him. Offered three judgments by the prophet Gad, he chose to fall into the hand of the Lord, and seventy thousand men died of the pestilence before the Lord stayed the angel at the threshing floor of Araunah, which David bought for an altar (2 Samuel 24:10-25).
offenseFull: Two accounts tell one event. Second Samuel says the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel and he moved David against them to number Israel and Judah (2 Samuel 24:1). First Chronicles says Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel (1 Chronicles 21:1). The teaching reconciles them: it is all saying the same thing. The Most High wanted to judge Israel, and he used David and used Satan to do it. Satan cannot come into a man’s life without the okay from God: God chooses him, and Satan uses him. The Lord already knew the lust that was in David, and it was Satan’s work to feed that desire and keep tempting him until he carried it out.

The lust was pride, the desire of a man in power to know how many he is over. Only God is supposed to know the number of his people. Numbering was not the king’s work but the Levites’, and when Israel was counted under the law, every man from twenty years old and up gave a ransom for his soul, half a shekel, rich and poor alike, so that no plague would come on them (Exodus 30:11-16). Joab tried to talk sense into the king. He asked why the king took delight in this thing when God already knew the number, but the king’s word prevailed against Joab and the captains of the host (2 Samuel 24:3-4). Chronicles adds that Joab called it a cause of trespass to Israel and left Levi and Benjamin uncounted, because the king’s word was abominable to him (1 Chronicles 21:3-6).

The count took nine months and twenty days from Dan to Beer-sheba, and Joab brought back eight hundred thousand valiant men of Israel who drew the sword and five hundred thousand of Judah, not counting the women and children (2 Samuel 24:5-9). The teaching sets this beside the census of today. The powers that control the earth count the people not for their good but to know what level of force to use against them. A leader aligned with God does as Joab said and keeps the number to God.
judgmentFull: As soon as it was done it hit him. David’s conscience struck him; he confessed that he had sinned greatly and done very foolishly, and asked the Lord to take away his servant’s iniquity (2 Samuel 24:10). In the morning the word came to Gad, David’s seer, with three judgments and a choice of one: famine in the land, three months fleeing before his enemies, or three days of pestilence (2 Samuel 24:11-13). Samuel gives the famine as seven years and Chronicles as three (1 Chronicles 21:11-12). David was in a great strait and chose to fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercies are great, rather than into the hand of man, knowing that man would not show him the mercy the Most High would (2 Samuel 24:14; 1 Chronicles 21:13).

The pestilence ran from the morning to the time appointed, and seventy thousand men died from Dan to Beer-sheba (2 Samuel 24:15). God killed seventy thousand because David decided to number the people, and the same way God used the nations back then to correct us when we were disobedient, it is the same thing today. The notes send the reader back to the first verse: the reason for the seventy thousand is that the Most High was angry at Israel. When the angel stretched out his hand over Jerusalem, the Lord repented of the evil and told him it was enough. David saw the angel, something we cannot see today, for this walk is by faith and the keeping of the commandments. He and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fell on their faces, and he pleaded that he alone had sinned and that the sheep had done nothing (2 Samuel 24:16-17; 1 Chronicles 21:16-17).

Gad sent him to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite. Araunah offered the floor, the oxen and the threshing tools as a free gift, but David would not offer the Lord burnt offerings that cost him nothing. He paid, built the altar, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the plague was stayed from Israel (2 Samuel 24:18-25). Samuel gives the price as fifty shekels of silver for the floor and the oxen; Chronicles gives six hundred shekels of gold for the place, and adds that the Lord answered by fire from heaven and the angel put up his sword (1 Chronicles 21:25-27). True worship costs us something. That threshing floor on mount Moriah is where Solomon later built the house of the Lord (2 Chronicles 3:1).

davids-census.offense: Two accounts tell one event. Second Samuel says the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel and he moved David against them to number Israel and Judah (2 Samuel 24:1). First Chronicles says Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David to number Israel (1 Chronicles 21:1). The teaching reconciles them: it is all saying the same thing. The Most High wanted to judge Israel, and he used David and used Satan to do it. Satan cannot come into a man’s life without the okay from God: God chooses him, and Satan uses him. The Lord already knew the lust that was in David, and it was Satan’s work to feed that desire and keep tempting him until he carried it out.

doeg-and-the-priests-of-nob.name: Saul and Doeg at Nob
doeg-and-the-priests-of-nob.charge: Slaughter of the priests of the Lord on an Edomite’s report
doeg-and-the-priests-of-nob.summary: Saul had set an Edomite over his servants. Doeg reported that Ahimelech had enquired of the Lord for David, given him the hallowed bread and the sword of Goliath, and Saul, who by then read any loyalty to David as treason against himself, would not hear the priest’s defence. The king’s own footmen would not put forth their hand against the priests of the Lord, so he got the Edomite to do what his own men would not: Doeg slew eighty-five men that wore a linen ephod and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword. David wrote the Edomite’s sentence in a psalm.
offenseFull: David came to Nob to Ahimelech the priest, three days out in the field and fearful of king Saul, and the priest gave him hallowed bread, for there was no bread there but the shewbread that had been taken from before the Lord (1 Samuel 21:6-7). Christ recounted this very history when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, asking whether they had never read what David did when he had need and was an hungred (Mark 2:25-26); precept it in your bibles if it is not there already. A certain servant of Saul was detained before the Lord that day: Doeg, an Edomite, the chief of Saul’s herdmen (1 Samuel 21:7). The scriptures tell us never to trust an enemy (Ecclesiasticus 12:10), yet here is a king of Israel with an Edomite set over his servants. Doeg answered and reported that he had seen the son of Jesse come to Nob to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, who enquired of the Lord for him, gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine (1 Samuel 22:9-10). Saul sent for Ahimelech and all his father’s house, the priests in Nob, and charged them with conspiracy; Ahimelech answered that no one among all the king’s servants was as faithful as David, the king’s son in law, who went at his bidding and was honourable in his house, and that it was hardly the first time he had enquired of God for him, and the king should impute nothing to his servant nor to all his father’s house (1 Samuel 22:13-16). Saul had become so desperate that he read loyalty to David as betrayal of himself, because he wanted everybody against David. That is no new thing under the sun: men put slander out to turn whole congregations against a man they have never sat down with and broken bread with.
judgmentFull: The king told the footmen standing about him to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, because their hand also was with David, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. So the king said to Doeg, turn and fall upon the priests; and Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon them and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, oxen, asses and sheep (1 Samuel 22:13-19). Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do. Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been on this man from the beginning: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and comforted himself with the purpose of slaying his brother (Genesis 27:41). That comfort in killing is the same thing seen in Doeg; when Saul appointed him to the task you can best believe he found pleasure in it. Eighty-five priests and a whole city destroyed because they showed affinity to David, all out of hatred and envy. The servant is not greater than his lord, and if they persecuted Christ they will persecute us (John 15:20), and not only by the heathen but by our own kinsmen.

One of the sons of Ahimelech, named Abiathar, escaped and fled after David, and told him that Saul had slain the Lord’s priests. David answered that he had known that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul, and that he had occasioned the death of all the persons of his father’s house; Abiathar was to abide with him and fear not, for the man who sought David’s life sought his life, and with David he would be in safeguard (1 Samuel 22:20-23). Where the reigning king had become a threat, the fugitive became a shelter.

Doeg’s own sentence is written in the psalm David made about him, the psalm inscribed for the day when Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul that David was come to the house of Ahimelech: his tongue devised mischief like a sharp razor, working deceitfully, loving evil more than good and lying rather than speaking righteousness; therefore God would likewise destroy him for ever, take him away, pluck him out of his dwelling place, and root him out of the land of the living (Psalms 52:5). David did not tell the Edomite he could come and rule with him in the kingdom. That is the sentence, and it stands over the nation Doeg came from.

Christ recounted this very history when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, asking whether they had never read what David did when he had need and was an hungred (Mark 2:25-26); precept it in your bibles if it is not there already. A certain servant of Saul was detained before the Lord that day: Doeg, an Edomite, the chief of Saul’s herdmen (1 Samuel 21:7). The scriptures tell us never to trust an enemy (Ecclesiasticus 12:10), yet here is a king of Israel with an Edomite set over his servants. Doeg answered and reported that he had seen the son of Jesse come to Nob to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, who enquired of the Lord for him, gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine (1 Samuel 22:9-10). Saul sent for Ahimelech and all his father’s house, the priests in Nob, and charged them with conspiracy; Ahimelech answered that no one among all the king’s servants was as faithful as David, the king’s son in law, who went at his bidding and was honourable in his house, and that it was hardly the first time he had enquired of God for him, and the king should impute nothing to his servant nor to all his father’s house (1 Samuel 22:13-16). Saul had become so desperate that he read loyalty to David as betrayal of himself, because he wanted everybody against David. That is no new thing under the sun: men put slander out to turn whole congregations against a man they have never sat down with and broken bread with.
doeg-and-the-priests-of-nob.judgment: The king told the footmen standing about him to turn and slay the priests of the Lord, because their hand also was with David, but the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord. So the king said to Doeg, turn and fall upon the priests; and Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon them and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod, and smote Nob, the city of the priests, with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, oxen, asses and sheep (1 Samuel 22:13-19). Saul was able to get the Edomite to do what his own men would not do. Go back to Genesis and see the spirit that has been on this man from the beginning: Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing, and comforted himself with the purpose of slaying his brother (Genesis 27:41). That comfort in killing is the same thing seen in Doeg; when Saul appointed him to the task you can best believe he found pleasure in it. Eighty-five priests and a whole city destroyed because they showed affinity to David, all out of hatred and envy. The servant is not greater than his lord, and if they persecuted Christ they will persecute us (John 15:20), and not only by the heathen but by our own kinsmen.

text.text: So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.
Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?
How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
Now a certain man of the servants of Saul was there that day, detained before the Lord; and his name was Doeg, an Edomite, the chiefest of the herdmen that belonged to Saul.
Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.
Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
And he enquired of the Lord for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?
Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.
And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the Lord; because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the Lord.

And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.
And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.
And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.
Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.
And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the Lord’s priests.
And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house.
Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.
God shall likewise destroy thee for ever, he shall take thee away, and pluck thee out of thy dwelling place, and root thee out of the land of the living. Selah.

eli-and-sons.name: Eli and his sons
eli-and-sons.charge: Sons of Belial in the priest’s office, strong-arming the offering of the Lord and lying with the women at the tabernacle door; and a father who honoured his sons above the Lord
eli-and-sons.summary: The sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they did not know the Lord. Levites and priests in the house of the Lord, doing the work of the Lord, and yet they did not know Him, because they kept the commandments only on the surface where men could see. They sent a servant with a three-pronged fork to take the priest’s portion raw before the fat was burned, by force if the man refused, so that men despised the offering of the Lord; and they lay with the women who served at the door of the tabernacle. Eli said something, but he took no action. In one day both sons died, the ark was taken, and the old man fell backward from his seat and broke his neck.
offenseFull: The sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they did not know the Lord (1 Samuel 2:12-17). They were the devil. Priests in the house of the Lord, they still did not know Him, because they kept the commandments on the surface where you can see it and not true in their spirit. They looked the part, the fringes, the beard, showing up on the sabbath day, and their spirit was not right with the Lord. Do not let that be you, Israel. The custom was that while a man’s sacrifice was boiling, the priest’s servant plunged a three-pronged fork into the pot and the priest took whatever it brought up. That is how the Lord took care of Levi, who had no land inheritance among the tribes; He provided for them out of Israel’s sacrifices, so that they needed nothing. But these men would not wait. Before the fat was even burned the servant demanded raw meat, by force if the worshipper objected. So the young men’s sin was very great before the Lord, for men came to despise the Lord’s offering. Devils serving in the house of the Lord, strong-arming the offerings of the people.

Eli was very old, and he heard everything his sons did to Israel, and that they lay with the women serving at the door of the tabernacle, the harlots hanging around the temple (1 Samuel 2:22-25). He asked why they did such things, and told them they were making the Lord’s people sin. The Levites were the leaders, so the people followed their actions, saying it must be all right, look at how they live in the temple. But the sons would not listen to their father, because the Lord meant to put them to death. Eli said something to his children, but he did not remove them from the priesthood. He did not go further than words, and you have to watch what happened to his children.
judgmentFull: A man of God reminded Eli that the Lord had chosen his father’s house out of all the tribes as priests and given it Israel’s offerings (1 Samuel 2:27-36). Why then did they scorn His sacrifices, and why did Eli honour his sons above Him? Take that into account: do you honour your children above what the Lord says to do? Can they do no wrong, even when they keep no commandments and never show up on the sabbath day while living grown under your roof? Joshua resolved that he and his house would serve the Lord (Joshua 24:15), and the Lord dealt with Abraham as He did knowing he would command his children and household after him to keep the way of the Lord (Genesis 18:19). The Lord had promised Eli’s house would serve before Him for ever, but now He said He would honour those who honour Him, and those who despise Him would be lightly esteemed. Lightly esteemed means He is not looking out for you: you are not thinking about me, so I am not thinking about you. He would cut off the strength of Eli’s house, so that no man in it would reach old age. Cutting off the arm is cutting off the strength, and the strength was his children. Why judge the generations after? Not because a son dies for his father; each son lives or dies by his own doings (Ezekiel 18:10-17). Because Eli did not reprove his sons, the generations after them were going to follow in the same footsteps.

The sign was that his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, would both die on one day, and the Lord would raise up a faithful priest who would act according to His heart and mind. That is the same man we all have to be, not leaning on our own understanding or our own emotions (Proverbs 3:5). Whoever was left in Eli’s house would come begging for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread: Levi had no inheritance of land, and cut off from the priesthood there was nothing left but to beg. The Lord confirmed it to the child Samuel: Eli’s house was judged because his sons disgraced themselves and he did not stop them, and Eli accepted it as the Lord’s will (1 Samuel 3:13-18). When the Philistines fought Israel again, thirty thousand Israelite soldiers fell, the ark was taken, and both sons of Eli were killed (1 Samuel 4:10-22). When the news reached Shiloh that the ark was taken, Eli fell backward off his seat, broke his neck and died, for he was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years. His daughter in law named her newborn Ichabod, for the glory had departed from Israel.

text.text: Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord.
And the priests’ custom with the people was, that, when any man offered sacrifice, the priest’s servant came, while the flesh was in seething, with a fleshhook of three teeth in his hand;
And he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fleshhook brought up the priest took for himself. So they did in Shiloh unto all the Israelites that came thither.
Also before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.

And if any man said unto him, Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth; then he would answer him, Nay; but thou shalt give it me now: and if not, I will take it by force.
Wherefore the sin of the young men was very great before the Lord: for men abhorred the offering of the Lord.
Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel; and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.
And he said unto them, Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people.
Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make the Lord’s people to transgress.

If one man sin against another, the judge shall judge him: but if a man sin against the Lord, who shall intreat for him? Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto the voice of their father, because the Lord would slay them.
And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?

And did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel?

Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?

Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.
And thou shalt see an enemy in my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel: and there shall not be an old man in thine house for ever.
And the man of thine, whom I shall not cut off from mine altar, shall be to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thine heart: and all the increase of thine house shall die in the flower of their age.
And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas; in one day they shall die both of them.
And I will raise me up a faithful priest, that shall do according to that which is in mine heart and in my mind: and I will build him a sure house; and he shall walk before mine anointed for ever.

And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left in thine house shall come and crouch to him for a piece of silver and a morsel of bread, and shall say, Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a piece of bread.

And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.

For I know him, that he will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the Lord, to do justice and judgment; that the Lord may bring upon Abraham that which he hath spoken of him.
If he beget a son that is a robber, a shedder of blood, and that doeth the like to any one of these things,
And that doeth not any of those duties, but even hath eaten upon the mountains, and defiled his neighbour’s wife,
Hath oppressed the poor and needy, hath spoiled by violence, hath not restored the pledge, and hath lifted up his eyes to the idols, hath committed abomination,
Hath given forth upon usury, and hath taken increase: shall he then live? he shall not live: he hath done all these abominations; he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him.
Now, lo, if he beget a son, that seeth all his father’s sins which he hath done, and considereth, and doeth not such like,
That hath not eaten upon the mountains, neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, hath not defiled his neighbour’s wife,
Neither hath oppressed any, hath not withholden the pledge, neither hath spoiled by violence, but hath given his bread to the hungry, and hath covered the naked with a garment,

That hath taken off his hand from the poor, that hath not received usury nor increase, hath executed my judgments, hath walked in my statutes; he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
For I have told him that I will judge his house for ever for the iniquity which he knoweth; because his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not.
And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli, that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be purged with sacrifice nor offering for ever.
And Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of the house of the Lord. And Samuel feared to shew Eli the vision.
Then Eli called Samuel, and said, Samuel, my son. And he answered, Here am I.

And he said, What is the thing that the Lord hath said unto thee? I pray thee hide it not from me: God do so to thee, and more also, if thou hide any thing from me of all the things that he said unto thee.
And Samuel told him every whit, and hid nothing from him. And he said, It is the Lord: let him do what seemeth him good.
And the Philistines fought, and Israel was smitten, and they fled every man into his tent: and there was a very great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.
And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.
And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent, and with earth upon his head.
And when he came, lo, Eli sat upon a seat by the wayside watching: for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city, and told it, all the city cried out.
And when Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, What meaneth the noise of this tumult? And the man came in hastily, and told Eli.
Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were dim, that he could not see.
And the man said unto Eli, I am he that came out of the army, and I fled to day out of the army. And he said, What is there done, my son?

And the messenger answered and said, Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there hath been also a great slaughter among the people, and thy two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God is taken.

And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

And his daughter in law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered: and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken, and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed; for her pains came upon her.
And about the time of her death the women that stood by her said unto her, Fear not; for thou hast born a son. But she answered not, neither did she regard it.
And she named the child I–chabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father in law and her husband.
And she said, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken.
And there came a man of God unto Eli, and said unto him, Thus saith the Lord, Did I plainly appear unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt in Pharaoh’s house?

And did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to offer upon mine altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? and did I give unto the house of thy father all the offerings made by fire of the children of Israel?

Wherefore kick ye at my sacrifice and at mine offering, which I have commanded in my habitation; and honourest thy sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel my people?

Wherefore the Lord God of Israel saith, I said indeed that thy house, and the house of thy father, should walk before me for ever: but now the Lord saith, Be it far from me; for them that honour me I will honour, and they that despise me shall be lightly esteemed.
Behold, the days come, that I will cut off thine arm, and the arm of thy father’s house, that there shall not be an old man in thine house.
And thou shalt see an enemy in my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel: and there shall not be an old man in thine house for ever.
And the man of thine, whom I shall not cut off from mine altar, shall be to consume thine eyes, and to grieve thine heart: and all the increase of thine house shall die in the flower of their age.
And this shall be a sign unto thee, that shall come upon thy two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas; in one day they shall die both of them.

elijah.name: Elijah
elijah.charge: As the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand: shutting the heaven by prayer, standing alone against eight hundred and fifty at Carmel, and running before the king in the hand of the Lord
elijah.summary: Elijah the Tishbite of Gilead stood before Ahab and declared, by the Lord God of Israel before whom he stood, that there would be no dew nor rain but by his word (1 Kings 17:1). The Lord fed him by ravens and by a widow of Zarephath, raised her son at his prayer, and at Carmel answered him by fire before all Israel and the prophets of Baal, then sent rain (1 Kings 17:2-24; 1 Kings 18:17-46). Fleeing Jezebel, he asked to die, but the Lord fed him, spoke to him at Horeb in a still small voice, told him seven thousand had not bowed to Baal, and gave him Elisha; he was taken up by a whirlwind (1 Kings 19:1-19; 2 Kings 2:11-13).
offenseFull: The session on these chapters frames everything on the power of the Most High, set on display through His prophet. Elijah told Ahab there would be no dew nor rain those years but according to his word; he prayed, and it did not rain (1 Kings 17:1). The history the class reads calls him a man of tempestuous nature, guided by no consideration of expediency, who thundered against the weak, woman-led Ahab and was gone before anyone could seize him; he wore a leather girdle and a hairy cloak, unlike the effeminate dress of the worshippers of Baal, and he was known by it (2 Kings 1:8). The Lord sent him to hide by the brook Cherith, where the ravens brought him bread and flesh morning and evening, for He can command the animals to feed a man (1 Kings 17:2-6). When the brook dried up He sent him to a widow at Zarephath, whose meal and oil did not fail, and at his prayer her dead son revived (1 Kings 17:7-22). She said that now she knew he was a man of God and the word of the Lord in his mouth was truth (1 Kings 17:24): a man of God is known because the word in his mouth is the word of truth.
In the third year he showed himself to Ahab, and when Ahab called him the troubler of Israel, he answered that Ahab and his father’s

house were, for forsaking the commandments and following Baalim (1 Kings 18:17-18). At Carmel he asked the people how long they would halt between two opinions; if the Lord is God, follow Him. They answered not a word (1 Kings 18:21). It is a call for us to examine ourselves and not keep one foot in and one foot out, for the lukewarm are spewed out (Revelation 3:15-16). The prophets of Baal cried from morning until past noon, leaped on their altar and cut themselves till the blood gushed out, and Elijah mocked them; no one answered, because the Lord will not give His glory to another and the gods of the nations are idols (1 Kings 18:26-29; Isaiah 42:8; Psalms 96:5). He repaired the altar of the Lord with twelve stones for the twelve tribes, drenched the sacrifice three times until the trench was full, and at the evening sacrifice prayed that the people would know the Lord is God in Israel and that He had turned their heart back again (1 Kings 18:30-37).
judgmentFull: The fire of the Lord fell and consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones and the dust, and licked up the water. The people fell on their faces crying that the Lord, He is the God, and at Elijah’s word the prophets of Baal were taken down to the brook Kishon and slain (1 Kings 18:38-40). The false shepherds of today stand under the same woe (Jeremiah 23:1-2). Then he prayed on the top of Carmel with his face between his knees until a cloud like a man’s hand rose from the sea, and there was a great rain; the hand of the Lord was on him and he ran before Ahab to Jezreel (1 Kings 18:41-46).

When Jezebel swore to take his life he fled, sat under a juniper tree, and asked to die, saying he was no better than his fathers (1 Kings 19:1-4). The notes say our forefathers had ultimate faith and understood regeneration, trusting the Most High to raise them when He chose. An angel fed him twice, and in the strength of that food he went forty days and nights to Horeb (1 Kings 19:5-8). The Lord passed by in wind, earthquake and fire, and was not in them, and then came a still small voice (1 Kings 19:11-12); we do not know who we are dealing with. He said he alone was left, and the Lord sent him to anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha in his place, and told him He had left Himself seven thousand in Israel who had not bowed to Baal (1 Kings 19:14-18). Elijah was not by himself; the Lord had people reserved who had not yet awakened, and the classes say that is why we pray for more labourers and preach, for we never know which flyer or video will wake one. He cast his mantle on Elisha (1 Kings 19:19), founded a circle of disciples who kept the ancient law alive, and was taken up by a whirlwind while Elisha cried after him as his father (2 Kings 2:11-13). Christ said Elias had come already, and the disciples understood He spoke of John the Baptist (Matthew 17:11-13), who came in his spirit before the great day (Malachi 4:5).

text.text: And Elijah the Tishbite, who was of the inhabitants of Gilead, said unto Ahab, As the Lord God of Israel liveth, before whom I stand, there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.
So he went and did according unto the word of the Lord: for he went and dwelt by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
And it came to pass after these things, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick; and his sickness was so sore, that there was no breath left in him.
And she said unto Elijah, What have I to do with thee, O thou man of God? art thou come unto me to call my sin to remembrance, and to slay my son?
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And Elijah took the child, and brought him down out of the chamber into the house, and delivered him unto his mother: and Elijah said, See, thy son liveth.
And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.
Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel unto mount Carmel, and the prophets of Baal four hundred and fifty, and the prophets of the groves four hundred, which eat at Jezebel’s table.
So Ahab sent unto all the children of Israel, and gathered the prophets together unto mount Carmel.
And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
Then said Elijah unto the people, I, even I only, remain a prophet of the Lord; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred and fifty men.

Let them therefore give us two bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under: and I will dress the other bullock, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under:
And call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord: and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered and said, It is well spoken.
And Elijah said unto the prophets of Baal, Choose you one bullock for yourselves, and dress it first; for ye are many; and call on the name of your gods, but put no fire under.

And they took the bullock which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, O Baal, hear us. But there was no voice, nor any that answered. And they leaped upon the altar which was made.

And it came to pass at noon, that Elijah mocked them, and said, Cry aloud: for he is a god; either he is talking, or he is pursuing, or he is in a journey, or peradventure he sleepeth, and must be awaked.
And they cried aloud, and cut themselves after their manner with knives and lancets, till the blood gushed out upon them.
And it came to pass, when midday was past, and they prophesied until the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that there was neither voice, nor any to answer, nor any that regarded.
And Elijah said unto all the people, Come near unto me. And all the people came near unto him. And he repaired the altar of the Lord that was broken down.
And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, unto whom the word of the Lord came, saying, Israel shall be thy name:
And with the stones he built an altar in the name of the Lord: and he made a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed.
And he put the wood in order, and cut the bullock in pieces, and laid him on the wood, and said, Fill four barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood.
And he said, Do it the second time. And they did it the second time. And he said, Do it the third time. And they did it the third time.
And the water ran round about the altar; and he filled the trench also with water.

And it came to pass at the time of the offering of the evening sacrifice, that Elijah the prophet came near, and said, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel, and that I am thy servant, and that I have done all these things at thy word.
Hear me, O Lord, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.
Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.
And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them: and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.
And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is a sound of abundance of rain.
So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees,
And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.
And it came to pass in the mean while, that the heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time.
And when he saw that, he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer–sheba, which belongeth to Judah, and left his servant there.

But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree: and he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O Lord, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.
And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.
And he looked, and, behold, there was a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.
And the angel of the Lord came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.
And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.
And he came thither unto a cave, and lodged there; and, behold, the word of the Lord came to him, and he said unto him, What doest thou here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And, behold, the Lord passed by, and a great and strong wind rent the mountains, and brake in pieces the rocks before the Lord; but the Lord was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the Lord was not in the earthquake:
And after the earthquake a fire; but the Lord was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice.

And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

And he said, I have been very jealous for the Lord God of hosts: because the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.
And the Lord said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria:
And Jehu the son of Nimshi shalt thou anoint to be king over Israel: and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel–meholah shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room.
And it shall come to pass, that him that escapeth the sword of Hazael shall Jehu slay: and him that escapeth from the sword of Jehu shall Elisha slay.
Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him.
So he departed thence, and found Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth: and Elijah passed by him, and cast his mantle upon him.

And it came to pass, as they still went on, and talked, that, behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.
And Elisha saw it, and he cried, My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof. And he saw him no more: and he took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces.
He took up also the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan;
And they answered him, He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins. And he said, It is Elijah the Tishbite.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Get thee hence, and turn thee eastward, and hide thyself by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.
So he went and did according unto the word of the Lord: for he went and dwelt by the brook Cherith, that is before Jordan.
And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.

And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.

And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.

And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
And the woman said to Elijah, Now by this I know that thou art a man of God, and that the word of the Lord in thy mouth is truth.
And it came to pass, when Ahab saw Elijah, that Ahab said unto him, Art thou he that troubleth Israel?
And he answered, I have not troubled Israel; but thou, and thy father’s house, in that ye have forsaken the commandments of the Lord, and thou hast followed Baalim.
And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.
I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot.
So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth.

Hear me, O Lord, hear me, that this people may know that thou art the Lord God, and that thou hast turned their heart back again.
Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench.
And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces: and they said, The Lord, he is the God; the Lord, he is the God.
And Elijah said unto them, Take the prophets of Baal; let not one of them escape. And they took them: and Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and slew them there.
Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.

Therefore thus saith the Lord God of Israel against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith the Lord.
And Elijah said unto Ahab, Get thee up, eat and drink; for there is a sound of abundance of rain.
So Ahab went up to eat and to drink. And Elijah went up to the top of Carmel; and he cast himself down upon the earth, and put his face between his knees,
And said to his servant, Go up now, look toward the sea. And he went up, and looked, and said, There is nothing. And he said, Go again seven times.

And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man’s hand. And he said, Go up, say unto Ahab, Prepare thy chariot, and get thee down, that the rain stop thee not.
And it came to pass in the mean while, that the heaven was black with clouds and wind, and there was a great rain. And Ahab rode, and went to Jezreel.
And the hand of the Lord was on Elijah; and he girded up his loins, and ran before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
And Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, and withal how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.
Then Jezebel sent a messenger unto Elijah, saying, So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time.
And when he saw that, he arose, and went for his life, and came to Beer–sheba, which belongeth to Judah, and left his servant there.

And he looked, and, behold, there was a cake baken on the coals, and a cruse of water at his head. And he did eat and drink, and laid him down again.
And the angel of the Lord came again the second time, and touched him, and said, Arise and eat; because the journey is too great for thee.
And he arose, and did eat and drink, and went in the strength of that meat forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God.

And he said, Go forth, and stand upon the mount before the Lord. And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the Lord be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

Let them therefore give us two bullocks; and let them choose one bullock for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under: and I will dress the other bullock, and lay it on wood, and put no fire under:
And call ye on the name of your gods, and I will call on the name of the Lord: and the God that answereth by fire, let him be God. And all the people answered and said, It is well spoken.

And it shall be, that thou shalt drink of the brook; and I have commanded the ravens to feed thee there.

And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.
And it came to pass after a while, that the brook dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.
And the word of the Lord came unto him, saying,
Arise, get thee to Zarephath, which belongeth to Zidon, and dwell there: behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee.

So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
And as she was going to fetch it, he called to her, and said, Bring me, I pray thee, a morsel of bread in thine hand.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.
And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son.
For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth.
And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
And he said unto her, Give me thy son. And he took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into a loft, where he abode, and laid him upon his own bed.
And he cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, hast thou also brought evil upon the widow with whom I sojourn, by slaying her son?
And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and cried unto the Lord, and said, O Lord my God, I pray thee, let this child’s soul come into him again.
And the Lord heard the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child came into him again, and he revived.
Seeing his days are determined, the number of his months are with thee, thou hast appointed his bounds that he cannot pass;

And he put the wood in order, and cut the bullock in pieces, and laid him on the wood, and said, Fill four barrels with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood.

And it was so, when Elijah heard it, that he wrapped his face in his mantle, and went out, and stood in the entering in of the cave. And, behold, there came a voice unto him, and said, What doest thou here, Elijah?

elisha.name: Elisha
elisha.charge: Leaving the oxen and following; asking a double portion of the spirit; and refusing Naaman’s reward, as the Lord liveth, before whom I stand
elisha.summary: Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and cast his mantle on him; Elisha killed his oxen, fed the people with them, and followed (1 Kings 19:19-21). He would not leave his master, asked for a double portion of his spirit, saw him taken up, and parted the Jordan with his mantle (2 Kings 2:1-15). The spirit of Elijah worked through him in healings, provision and deliverance; he refused Naaman’s gifts, and after his death a dead man who touched his bones revived (2 Kings 5:15-16; 2 Kings 13:20-21).
offenseFull: Elijah passed by Elisha the son of Shaphat, who was plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and cast his mantle on him without a word. Elisha left the oxen, ran after him, and asked to kiss his father and mother first. Then he went back, killed a yoke of oxen, boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, gave it to the people, and went after Elijah and ministered to him (1 Kings 19:19-21). The Mantle class draws the lesson. The mantle was the prophets’ garment, and the spirit in Elisha told him this was a special calling. He had faith: husbandry was his living, yet he destroyed the oxen and the instruments and did not turn back. No man who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom (Luke 9:57-62). Twelve oxen under one goad are the twelve tribes, and guiding them takes the tunnel vision of a straight furrow, and the class asks where that faith is in brothers today who give up their post when home life pulls at them.

When the Lord was about to take Elijah up, at Gilgal, Bethel and Jericho Elijah told him to stay behind, and each time Elisha swore he would not leave him. The sons of the prophets, a prophetic order and not blood sons, told him his master would be taken, and he told them he knew it. Elijah struck the Jordan with his mantle and they crossed on dry ground, and when Elijah asked what he should do for him, Elisha asked for a double portion of his spirit (2 Kings 2:1-10). He saw him go up in a whirlwind with a chariot and horses of fire, cried after him as his father, took up the mantle that fell from him, struck the waters, and they parted; the sons of the prophets said the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha and bowed before him (2 Kings 2:11-15). Walking in Elijah’s Footsteps, reading the history of the prophetic schools, says Elisha then placed himself at the head of Elijah’s disciples at Bethel, Gilgal and Jericho, lived at first on Mount Carmel, and later roused the man who destroyed the house of Omri and ended the worship of Baal.
judgmentFull: The spirit that was on Elijah worked through him where the people were in need. He healed Jericho’s waters with salt (2 Kings 2:19-22). For a widow of the sons of the prophets whose sons were to be taken for her dead husband’s debt, the oil ran until every borrowed vessel was full, and she paid the debt and lived on the rest (2 Kings 4:1-7). The Shunammite who made him a chamber bore a son at his word, and when the child died, Elisha shut the door, prayed, and stretched himself on him until he sneezed seven times and opened his eyes (2 Kings 4:8-37). He took the death out of the pot at Gilgal and fed a hundred men with twenty loaves, with some left over, according to the word of the Lord (2 Kings 4:38-44).

When Naaman the Syrian was cleansed and came back confessing that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel, Elisha swore by the Lord before whom he stood that he would receive nothing, though Naaman urged him (2 Kings 5:15-16). Gehazi ran after the gifts and went out a leper, for that was not the time to receive (2 Kings 5:20-27; Ecclesiastes 3:6). When Syria sent a host by night to Dothan for one prophet, he told his servant that those with them were more than those against them, and the Lord opened the young man’s eyes to a mountain full of horses and chariots of fire; the angel of the Lord encamps round those who fear Him (2 Kings 6:15-17; Psalms 34:7). He led the blinded Syrians into Samaria and had them fed and sent home, and their raids stopped (2 Kings 6:18-23).

On his deathbed King Joash wept over him as the chariot of Israel, and Elisha put his hands on the king’s hands for the arrow of the Lord’s deliverance from Syria; the king struck the ground only three times, and Elisha was angry, for he would now beat Syria only three times (2 Kings 13:14-19). Elisha died and was buried, and when a dead man was thrown into his sepulchre and touched his bones, he revived and stood on his feet (2 Kings 13:20-21). History in the AM reads Sirach on him: filled with Elijah’s spirit, he was not moved by any prince, no one could bring him into subjection, and after his death his body prophesied (Ecclesiasticus 48:12-14).
