taught.title: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

text.text: For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.
But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:
For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.
Knowing that shortly I must put off this my tabernacle, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath shewed me.
And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:
Save that the Holy Ghost witnesseth in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.
Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labours more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths oft.
Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.
Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;

In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by mine own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
Beside those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.
And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead.
Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and came into the city: and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such an one caught up to the third heaven.
And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)
How that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
For I am the least of the apostles, that am not meet to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
But by the grace of God I am what I am: and his grace which was bestowed upon me was not in vain; but I laboured more abundantly than they all: yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,
I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain.
And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible.
I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air:
But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection: lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.
I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.
Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee: for he is profitable to me for the ministry.
Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work, and will preserve me unto his heavenly kingdom: to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I have coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.
Yea, ye yourselves know, that these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
I have shewed you all things, how that so labouring ye ought to support the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how he said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

peter-at-antioch.name: Peter at Antioch
peter-at-antioch.charge: Dissembling: withdrawing from the Gentiles for fear of them of the circumcision
peter-at-antioch.summary: At Antioch Peter had eaten with the Gentiles until certain men came from James, and then he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews dissembled with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away. Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed, and said before them all that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel. This history is not recorded in Acts; Paul tells it himself to the Galatians.
offenseFull: When James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace given to Paul, they gave him and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship, that they should go to the heathen and the pillars to the circumcision (Galatians 2:9). The heathen there is the northern kingdom, the same people called the Gentiles and the uncircumcision; the scripture itself calls the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali Galilee of the Gentiles, and those are two tribes of Israel (Matthew 4:15-16). Paul was already at Antioch doing his ministry when Peter came along later. But when Peter was come to Antioch, Paul withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed; for before certain men came from James he did eat with the Gentiles, and when they were come he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision, and the other Jews dissembled likewise with him, so that even Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation (Galatians 2:11-13). This history is not recorded in Acts at all. Peter was the head apostle, second in command from Christ, and he still made mistakes.

Four words carry the charge: he withdrew, he separated himself, the others dissembled, and Barnabas was carried away with their dissimulation. To dissimulate is to disguise or conceal under a false appearance, to hide the real motive behind a pretense; dissimulation is feigning and hypocrisy. In plain speech, Peter was being fake, and the reason given is fear. The men he had been eating with were Israelites of the northern kingdom living in a Gentile way of life; when

the southern kingdom arrived he separated himself from them out of respect of persons, not wanting to be seen eating with them, and Barnabas withdrew with him and would not sit or eat with them either. That withdrawing is the very thing that broke the nation in the first place, when the ten tribes told Rehoboam they had no portion in David and every man went to his tent (1 Kings 12:16). The law forbids respect of persons in judgment, neither respecting the person of the poor nor honouring the person of the mighty (Leviticus 19:15). And Peter knew better than any man there, because he was the one who had been told by God not to call any man common or unclean, and the one who had watched the same gift of the Holy Ghost fall on that household (Acts 10:28, Acts 11:2-3, Acts 15:7-9).
judgmentFull: When Paul saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, he said to Peter before them all that if he, being a Jew, lived after the manner of Gentiles and not as do the Jews, he had no business compelling the Gentiles to live as do the Jews (Galatians 2:14). Paul confronted him in front of everybody. The charge was plain: you claim to be a Jew, salvation is of the Jews, you are supposed to be the example, and you are following their footsteps instead of setting one, showing respect of persons and living like them while trying to teach them to follow after the Jews. You are being a hypocrite in your actions. Paul did not let things slide; he had no respect of persons and feared no man regardless of his status. You already learned this, Peter. God showed you that you cannot call any man common or unclean. You sat with them, and you convinced many of the Jews that these men were all right, and now you are wavering.

The correction went no further than the rebuke. Galatians records no sentence taking Peter out of his work, and the next words of the letter are Paul including himself with him: we who are Jews by nature, knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ (Galatians 2:15-16). Peter was corrected in front of them all and would have been embarrassed and ashamed, and he repented; and as a teacher, what does a man teach after that? What he repented from. Do not be fake. Reproof between brethren is the law and not an injury, since the commandment is to rebuke a brother plainly and not to hate him in the heart (Leviticus 19:17), and Peter himself afterward wrote of the wisdom given to our beloved brother Paul (2 Peter 3:15-16). The case is kept in the book so that a so-called Christian cannot use it to excuse breaking the commandments, and so that a man with rank among us knows that rank is no cover for hypocrisy.

lawsResolved.text: Do not be hypocritical in serving God or in living a godly life.
We are not to have hypocritical leaders because they ensnare the people.
You are not to be partial towards anyone or a respecter of persons in exacting justice, whether they be poor or rich, small or great.
If your brother trespass against you, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.
We are exhorted to reprove, rebuke and correct with authority, patience and instruction.
You should not refuse to be corrected and reproved by the righteous among you.

text.text: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.
But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.
For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.
And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
Ye shall do no unrighteousness in judgment: thou shalt not respect the person of the poor, nor honour the person of the mighty: but in righteousness shalt thou judge thy neighbour.

And he said unto them, Ye know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but God hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.
And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
Saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.

And when there had been much disputing, Peter rose up, and said unto them, Men and brethren, ye know how that a good while ago God made choice among us, that the Gentiles by my mouth should hear the word of the gospel, and believe.
And God, which knoweth the hearts, bare them witness, giving them the Holy Ghost, even as he did unto us;
And put no difference between us and them, purifying their hearts by faith.

But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?
We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.
And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you;

As also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; in which are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.
Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:
But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.

peters-denial.name: Peter’s denial
peters-denial.charge: Denying Christ three times with cursing and swearing
peters-denial.summary: Peter said that though all men should be offended because of him he would never be offended, and that though he should die with him he would not deny him (Matthew 26:33-35). In the high priest’s hall he denied it to a damsel, then with an oath, and then with cursing and swearing that he did not know the man, and the cock crew (Matthew 26:69-75). The Lord turned and looked on Peter, and he remembered the word that had been spoken to him, and went out and wept bitterly (Luke 22:60-62).
offenseFull: Before the denial he was warned and he was prayed for. Satan had desired to have them, to sift them as wheat, and Christ told Peter he had prayed for him that his faith fail not, and that when he was converted he should strengthen his brethren (Luke 22:31-32). Peter had walked with him and was not yet converted. What converts a man is named in the psalm: the law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul (Psalms 19:7), and that is also what he was to strengthen his brethren with. Peter answered out of his own confidence that he was ready to go both into prison and to death, and was told what he would do before the cock crew (Luke 22:33-34). A man does not know tomorrow, for his life is a vapour that appears for a little time and then vanishes away (James 4:14-15).

He denied three times. The third time he was picked out by his speech, because he was a Galilaean; the way he talked gave him away, so that he sounded like the man he was denying (Luke 22:54-60). Matthew records the oath, and then the cursing and swearing that he did not know the man (Matthew 26:69-75). The warning about that stands in the same gospel: whoever confesses him before men, him will he confess before his Father, and whoever denies him before men will be denied (Matthew 10:32-33). It was the hour given to the other side, as Christ told the chief priests and the captains of the temple when they came out against him with swords and staves, that this was their hour and the power of darkness (Luke 22:52-53). Isaiah had written it plainly of the servant: he was despised and rejected of men, and we hid as it were our faces from him, and we esteemed him not (Isaiah 53:3). That verse is Peter in the courtyard.
judgmentFull: The look and the tears are the first part of the answer. The Lord turned and looked on Peter, and Peter remembered the word and went out and wept bitterly (Luke 22:60-62). The difference between this case and the traitor in the same chapter is what came after the weeping. When Judas saw what he had done he did not go back and reconcile; he went and hanged himself (Matthew 27:3-5). Peter reconciled. Godly sorrow works repentance to salvation, but the sorrow of the world works death (2 Corinthians 7:10).

The reconciliation is recorded. After the resurrection Christ asked Peter three times whether he loved him and three times charged him to feed his lambs and his sheep, once for each denial, and Peter was grieved at the third asking (John 21:15-17). Then he was told by what death he should glorify God, that when he was old another would gird him and carry him where he would not (John 21:18-19), which answers what he had been told in the upper room, that where Christ was going he could not follow then but should follow afterwards (John 13:36). The history says he was held nine months in prison at Rome, converted the keepers and others while he was in there, and was scourged and crucified with his head downward, a position he asked for because he did not count himself worthy to die as his master died. The man who bounced back from that courtyard is the same man who stood at the gate called Beautiful and told a lame beggar that he had no silver and gold, but gave him what he had (Acts 3:1-8). The charge given with the warning stood: once converted, he was to strengthen his brethren. The fall did not cancel the man, and it did not cancel what he was sent to teach.

text.text: Peter answered and said unto him, Though all men shall be offended because of thee, yet will I never be offended.
Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
Peter said unto him, Though I should die with thee, yet will I not deny thee. Likewise also said all the disciples.
Now Peter sat without in the palace: and a damsel came unto him, saying, Thou also wast with Jesus of Galilee.
But he denied before them all, saying, I know not what thou sayest.
And when he was gone out into the porch, another maid saw him, and said unto them that were there, This fellow was also with Jesus of Nazareth.
And again he denied with an oath, I do not know the man.
And after a while came unto him they that stood by, and said to Peter, Surely thou also art one of them; for thy speech bewrayeth thee.
Then began he to curse and to swear, saying, I know not the man. And immediately the cock crew.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, which said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice. And he went out, and wept bitterly.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat:
But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.
And he said unto him, Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.
And he said, I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away.
For that ye ought to say, If the Lord will, we shall live, and do this, or that.
Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.
And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
Then Jesus said unto the chief priests, and captains of the temple, and the elders, which were come to him, Be ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and staves?
When I was daily with you in the temple, ye stretched forth no hands against me: but this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.
And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.

Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
Simon Peter said unto him, Lord, whither goest thou? Jesus answered him, Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.
And a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms.
And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us.
And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.
Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.
And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.
And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
And he cometh unto the disciples, and findeth them asleep, and saith unto Peter, What, could ye not watch with me one hour?
Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.

pharaoh-and-abimelech-with-sarah.name: Pharaoh and Abimelech, who took Sarah
pharaoh-and-abimelech-with-sarah.charge: Taking another man’s wife into the king’s house
pharaoh-and-abimelech-with-sarah.summary: Twice Abraham called Sarah his sister, and twice a king took her into his house. The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues; to Abimelech he came in a dream by night and told him he was a dead man, because the woman he had taken was a man’s wife. Adultery was sin in Genesis, long before Sinai, and the word spoken over Abraham, that the Most High would curse him that cursed him, worked here: a household plagued and every womb closed over the prophet’s wife.
offenseFull: Entering Egypt, Abram feared that the men of the place would kill him for his wife’s sake, for Sarai was a very fair woman to look upon even in her sixties, and he told her to say she was his sister; Pharaoh’s princes commended her and she was taken into Pharaoh’s house (Genesis 12:10-15). Years later in Gerar, with Sarah still that fair at ninety, Abimelech king of Gerar sent and took her on the same word (Genesis 20:1-2). She was in fact his sister, the daughter of his father but not the daughter of his mother, and the saying was their standing agreement in every strange land (Genesis 20:12-13). The laws that name such a marriage a wicked thing were written down through Moses some four hundred years after this (Leviticus 20:17; Deuteronomy 27:22).

Adultery was sin in Genesis, long before the seventh commandment was written at Sinai. God came to Abimelech in a dream by night and told him he was but a dead man, for the woman he had taken was a man’s wife; and the Most High said that he had withheld him from sinning against him, and suffered him not to touch her (Genesis 20:3-6). Abimelech called it what it is, a great sin, one of the weightier matters, for which there is no animal sacrifice that atones (Genesis 20:9). Abraham had thought the fear of God was not in that place (Genesis 20:11). The king was told to restore the man his wife, because the man was a prophet and would pray for him; and that if he did not restore her he would surely die, he and all that were his (Genesis 20:7).
judgmentFull: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh called Abram and sent him away with his wife and all that he had; and Abram came up out of Egypt very rich in cattle, in silver and in gold, so that the very household the wrong was done in paid for it (Genesis 12:17-20; Genesis 13:1-2). Behind the scenes with Abimelech the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of his house because of Sarah; the king restored her with sheep, oxen, servants and a thousand pieces of silver, Abraham prayed, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his maidservants, and they bare children (Genesis 20:14-18).

It happened both times she was taken, which is the point. The word given over Abraham was that the Most High would bless them that blessed him and curse him that cursed him, and here is that word working on two kings in two countries (Genesis 12:3). The Most High plagues a household over his prophet’s wife, and he does not play about it. The marriage stood under his protection whatever account the man had given of it, and neither king got past a dream and a plague before he let her go.

text.text: And there was a famine in the land: and Abram went down into Egypt to sojourn there; for the famine was grievous in the land.
And it came to pass, when he was come near to enter into Egypt, that he said unto Sarai his wife, Behold now, I know that thou art a fair woman to look upon:
Therefore it shall come to pass, when the Egyptians shall see thee, that they shall say, This is his wife: and they will kill me, but they will save thee alive.
Say, I pray thee, thou art my sister: that it may be well with me for thy sake; and my soul shall live because of thee.
And it came to pass, that, when Abram was come into Egypt, the Egyptians beheld the woman that she was very fair.
The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh: and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
And Abraham journeyed from thence toward the south country, and dwelled between Kadesh and Shur, and sojourned in Gerar.
And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.
And yet indeed she is my sister; she is the daughter of my father, but not the daughter of my mother; and she became my wife.

And it came to pass, when God caused me to wander from my father’s house, that I said unto her, This is thy kindness which thou shalt shew unto me; at every place whither we shall come, say of me, He is my brother.

And if a man shall take his sister, his father’s daughter, or his mother’s daughter, and see her nakedness, and she see his nakedness; it is a wicked thing; and they shall be cut off in the sight of their people: he hath uncovered his sister’s nakedness; he shall bear his iniquity.
Cursed be he that lieth with his sister, the daughter of his father, or the daughter of his mother. And all the people shall say, Amen.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream by night, and said to him, Behold, thou art but a dead man, for the woman which thou hast taken; for she is a man’s wife.
But Abimelech had not come near her: and he said, Lord, wilt thou slay also a righteous nation?
Said he not unto me, She is my sister? and she, even she herself said, He is my brother: in the integrity of my heart and innocency of my hands have I done this.
And God said unto him in a dream, Yea, I know that thou didst this in the integrity of thy heart; for I also withheld thee from sinning against me: therefore suffered I thee not to touch her.

Now therefore restore the man his wife; for he is a prophet, and he shall pray for thee, and thou shalt live: and if thou restore her not, know thou that thou shalt surely die, thou, and all that are thine.

Then Abimelech called Abraham, and said unto him, What hast thou done unto us? and what have I offended thee, that thou hast brought on me and on my kingdom a great sin? thou hast done deeds unto me that ought not to be done.
And Abraham said, Because I thought, Surely the fear of God is not in this place; and they will slay me for my wife’s sake.
And the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.
And Pharaoh called Abram, and said, What is this that thou hast done unto me? why didst thou not tell me that she was thy wife?
Why saidst thou, She is my sister? so I might have taken her to me to wife: now therefore behold thy wife, take her, and go thy way.
And Pharaoh commanded his men concerning him: and they sent him away, and his wife, and all that he had.
And Abram went up out of Egypt, he, and his wife, and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the south.
And Abram was very rich in cattle, in silver, and in gold.
And Abimelech took sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and womenservants, and gave them unto Abraham, and restored him Sarah his wife.
And Abimelech said, Behold, my land is before thee: dwell where it pleaseth thee.

And unto Sarah he said, Behold, I have given thy brother a thousand pieces of silver: behold, he is to thee a covering of the eyes, unto all that are with thee, and with all other: thus she was reproved.
So Abraham prayed unto God: and God healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bare children.
For the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech, because of Sarah Abraham’s wife.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
Thou shalt not commit adultery.

rachel-and-the-teraphim.name: Rachel and the stolen teraphim
rachel-and-the-teraphim.charge: Stealing her father’s images, and hiding them under her while she sat upon them
rachel-and-the-teraphim.summary: Rachel stole the images that were her father’s, hid them in the camel’s furniture and sat upon them, and told her father she could not rise up before him, so he searched and found them not. Jacob, not knowing, had said that whoever was found with them should not live. No sentence for the theft is announced. The strange gods stayed hidden in the household until Jacob commanded them put away before Bethel, and the beguiling of the mothers from Eve to Rachel is the warning the record leaves.
offenseFull: When Laban went to shear his sheep, Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s (Genesis 31:19). Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman that fears the Lord shall be praised: she was fine, and she was a thief (Proverbs 31:30). Laban’s own question, why he had stolen his gods, tells what house she came out of: an idolater of the line of Nahor, whose fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and that is why the Most High had told Abram to get out from his country and from his kindred (Genesis 31:30; Joshua 24:2).

Jacob, who did not know that Rachel had stolen them, answered that with whoever his gods were found, let him not live, and invited Laban to search before their brethren (Genesis 31:32). She had taken the images and put them in the camel’s furniture and sat upon them, and said to her father, let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before you, for the custom of women is upon me; and he searched all the tent and found not the images (Genesis 31:34-35). Idolatry was carried hidden into the covenant household, and a lie covered it, and her own husband had unknowingly pronounced a sentence over her head.
judgmentFull: No sentence for the theft is recorded, and Jacob’s oath was spoken in ignorance. The images stayed in the camp. Before going up to Bethel, Jacob said to his household and to all that were with him, put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments; the strange gods were there because she had stolen them and hidden them, and she gave them up then, and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem (Genesis 35:1-4). Idolatry hidden in a household has to be put away before a man can stand at Bethel.

What followed was protection, not punishment: the terror of God was upon the cities round about, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob, for the angel of the Lord encamps round about them that fear him and delivers them (Genesis 35:5; Psalms 34:7). From Eve to Rachel the scriptures show how sin comes into a house through the household, for of the woman came the beginning of sin, and the warning left here is for the mothers of Israel to guard against the same beguiling (Ecclesiasticus 25:24). Rachel died in hard labour bearing Benjamin in the way to Ephrath, which is Bethlehem, and Jacob set a pillar upon her grave (Genesis 35:16-20); the record does not name that death as the penalty for the theft, and it is not given as one. Delay is not acquittal.

text.text: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s.
Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.
And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.
With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.
And God said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth–el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto God, that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.
Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
And let us arise, and go up to Beth–el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and all their earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.
And they journeyed from Beth–el; and there was but a little way to come to Ephrath: and Rachel travailed, and she had hard labour.
And it came to pass, when she was in hard labour, that the midwife said unto her, Fear not; thou shalt have this son also.
And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Ben–oni: but his father called him Benjamin.
And Rachel died, and was buried in the way to Ephrath, which is Beth–lehem.
And Jacob set a pillar upon her grave: that is the pillar of Rachel’s grave unto this day.
And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone, because thou sore longedst after thy father’s house, yet wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?
And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid: for I said, Peradventure thou wouldest take by force thy daughters from me.
With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live: before our brethren discern thou what is thine with me, and take it to thee. For Jacob knew not that Rachel had stolen them.
And Laban went into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the two maidservants’ tents; but he found them not. Then went he out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.
Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them. And Laban searched all the tent, but found them not.
And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up before thee; for the custom of women is upon me. And he searched, but found not the images.

rebekah.name: Rebekah and Abraham’s servant
rebekah.charge: Abraham: making his servant swear to take no wife for Isaac of the daughters of the Canaanites. The servant: asking a sign at the well and worshipping when it came to pass. Rebekah: drawing for the camels, saying, I will go, and covering herself with a vail
rebekah.summary: Abraham, old and blessed in all things, made the eldest servant of his house swear by the Lord that he would take no wife for Isaac of the daughters of the Canaanites among whom he dwelt, but go to his own country and kindred. The servant asked a sign at the well, and before he had done speaking Rebekah came out, gave him drink and drew for all his camels, and he bowed his head and worshipped. Her family inquired at her own mouth whether she would go, and she said she would; when she saw Isaac she lighted off the camel and covered herself with a vail. Isaac brought her into his mother’s tent, and she became his wife, and he loved her.
offenseFull: Abraham was old and well stricken in age, and the Lord had blessed him in all things; he made the eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all he had, swear by the Lord, the God of heaven and earth, that he would not take a wife for his son of the daughters of the Canaanites among whom he dwelt, but go to his own country and kindred (Genesis 24:1-4). The Most High never condoned marrying into the other nations; the custom was kept from the beginning, long before Moses wrote the law, and the law states its own reason, that they turn the son away from following the Lord to serve other gods (Deuteronomy 7:3-4). Solomon is the prime example: he loved women of the other nations, went after their gods, and had to repent. Tobit says the same to his son: take a wife of the seed of your fathers, as Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob did from the beginning, and their seed shall inherit the land (Tobit 4:12). The forefathers arranged marriages, because the building block of a strong nation is a strong family, and a strong family comes from marriage, not from young people left to their own accord. Abraham told the servant that the Lord God of heaven, who swore to give the land to his seed, would send his angel before him (Genesis 24:7).

At the well the servant prayed for good speed and for kindness to his master, and asked a sign: let the damsel who, being asked to let down her pitcher, answered that she would give his camels drink also be the one appointed for Isaac (Genesis 24:12-14). Before he had done speaking, Rebekah came out, born to Bethuel the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder, very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: undefiled and beautiful, the kind of wife the forefathers had from the beginning (Genesis 24:15-16). He ran to meet her and asked to drink a little water; she hasted, let down her pitcher and gave him drink, then said she would draw for his camels also, and emptied her pitcher into the trough and ran again to the well (Genesis 24:17-20). She gave a stranger drink and then watered ten camels; that kind and easily entreated spirit is the pattern for the daughters of Israel. When the sign came to pass exactly, the man bowed his head and worshipped, and blessed the God of his master, who had not left him destitute of his mercy and his truth: being in the way, the Lord had led
him to the house of his master’s brethren (Genesis 24:26-27).

Her family asked to keep her ten days, and the servant said not to hinder him, seeing the Lord had prospered his way; so they called Rebekah and inquired at her own mouth whether she would go, and she said, I will go (Genesis 24:55-58). They sent their sister away with her nurse and blessed her: to be the mother of thousands of millions, and that her seed might possess the gate of those which hate them, which is the blessing of Israel and a prophecy (Genesis 24:59-60). Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide, a custom of the forefathers showing the Lord dealt with them long before Sinai (Genesis 24:63). When she saw him she lighted off the camel, and when the servant told her it was his master, she took a vail and covered herself (Genesis 24:64-65). The four mothers covered their heads with actual material as a sign of submission; the power a woman has upon her head is her obedience, the custom the apostle goes into (1 Corinthians 11:5-10).
judgmentFull: The servant told Isaac all things that he had done, and Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her, and he was comforted after his mother’s death, for he received a righteous wife like his mother (Genesis 24:66-67). He was forty when he took her; brothers waiting on a wife can be patient, because the right sister was appointed (Genesis 25:20).

When she was barren, Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife, and the Lord was entreated of him, and Rebekah conceived (Genesis 25:21). A barren sister is not to nag her husband but to pray, and a husband is to pray for his wife, because only the Lord opens a womb. The oath against the daughters of Canaan, the sign at the well and the woman who said she would go were all answered inside one house. And the covenant narrows again here: it runs through her children, and of her two sons it is Jacob who carries it.

text.text: And Abraham was old, and well stricken in age: and the Lord had blessed Abraham in all things.
And Abraham said unto his eldest servant of his house, that ruled over all that he had, Put, I pray thee, thy hand under my thigh:
And I will make thee swear by the Lord, the God of heaven, and the God of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:
But thou shalt go unto my country, and to my kindred, and take a wife unto my son Isaac.
And the servant said unto him, Peradventure the woman will not be willing to follow me unto this land: must I needs bring thy son again unto the land from whence thou camest?
And Abraham said unto him, Beware thou that thou bring not my son thither again.

The Lord God of heaven, which took me from my father’s house, and from the land of my kindred, and which spake unto me, and that sware unto me, saying, Unto thy seed will I give this land; he shall send his angel before thee, and thou shalt take a wife unto my son from thence.
And if the woman will not be willing to follow thee, then thou shalt be clear from this my oath: only bring not my son thither again.
And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master, and sware to him concerning that matter.
Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father’s tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
And the servant took ten camels of the camels of his master, and departed; for all the goods of his master were in his hand: and he arose, and went to Mesopotamia, unto the city of Nahor.
And he made his camels to kneel down without the city by a well of water at the time of the evening, even the time that women go out to draw water.
And he said, O Lord God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good speed this day, and shew kindness unto my master Abraham.
Behold, I stand here by the well of water; and the daughters of the men of the city come out to draw water:

And let it come to pass, that the damsel to whom I shall say, Let down thy pitcher, I pray thee, that I may drink; and she shall say, Drink, and I will give thy camels drink also: let the same be she that thou hast appointed for thy servant Isaac; and thereby shall I know that thou hast shewed kindness unto my master.
And it came to pass, before he had done speaking, that, behold, Rebekah came out, who was born to Bethuel, son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham’s brother, with her pitcher upon her shoulder.
And the damsel was very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well, and filled her pitcher, and came up.
And the servant ran to meet her, and said, Let me, I pray thee, drink a little water of thy pitcher.
And she said, Drink, my lord: and she hasted, and let down her pitcher upon her hand, and gave him drink.
And when she had done giving him drink, she said, I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.

And it came to pass, as the camels had done drinking, that the man took a golden earring of half a shekel weight, and two bracelets for her hands of ten shekels weight of gold;

And she said unto him, I am the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, which she bare unto Nahor.

And the man bowed down his head, and worshipped the Lord.
And he said, Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who hath not left destitute my master of his mercy and his truth: I being in the way, the Lord led me to the house of my master’s brethren.

rehoboam.name: Rehoboam
rehoboam.charge: Forsaking the counsel of the old men for the young men he grew up with; and forsaking the law of the Lord when the kingdom was established
rehoboam.summary: All Israel came to Shechem to make Solomon’s son king and asked him to lighten the heavy yoke his father had laid on them (1 Kings 12:1-4). Rehoboam forsook the counsel of the old men who had served Solomon, took the counsel of the young men he grew up with, and answered the people roughly, and ten tribes left the house of David that day, for the cause was from the Lord (1 Kings 12:6-20). Once his kingdom was strong he forsook the law of the Lord and all Israel with him, and Shishak of Egypt came up against Jerusalem until king and princes humbled themselves (2 Chronicles 12:1-12).
offenseFull: Sirach names him plainly: Solomon left behind him even the foolishness of the people, one that had no understanding, who turned away the people through his counsel (Ecclesiasticus 47:23). Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel came to make him king; Jeroboam came back from Egypt, and the congregation asked Rehoboam to lighten the grievous service and heavy yoke his father had put on them, and they would serve him (1 Kings 12:1-4). The study notes say the yoke was the labour of the building; Solomon did not enslave his own people as he did the nations, but they had to put in that work. Our Hidden History reads it as the taxes Solomon laid on the people to finance his wives’ temples.

He told them to come back in three days, which was wisdom, for it is right to take time and get counsel before giving an answer (1 Kings 12:5). He consulted the old men who had stood before Solomon, and they told him that if he would be a servant to the people that day and speak good words to them, they would be his servants forever. He forsook their counsel and turned to the young men who had grown up with him (1 Kings 12:6-8). Solomon was the wisest man on earth and still had counsellors, yet Rehoboam forsook the counsellors of the wisest man for his peers; the problem is getting counsel from those on your own level rather than from your elders. The classes call it pride, and add that his father, busy with his own pleasures, had not been there to guide him. The young men told him to say that his little finger would be thicker than his father’s loins, and that where his father chastised them with whips he would chastise them with scorpions (1 Kings 12:9-11). On the third day he spoke to the people roughly in just those words (1 Kings 12:12-14). You are where you are based on the decisions you made.

The study notes on Chronicles show the second offense. When Rehoboam had established the kingdom and strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him (2 Chronicles 12:1). One who leads goes astray and carries many with him. Judah built high places, images and groves on every high hill, and sodomites were in the land (1 Kings 14:22-24). He did evil because he did not prepare his heart to seek the Lord (2 Chronicles 12:14); Solomon had prepared his heart at Gibeon, and his son did not follow those footsteps.
judgmentFull: The king did not listen to the people, for the cause was from the Lord, that the word spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam might come to pass (1 Kings 12:15). Israel answered that they had no portion in David, and went to their tents; Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, and all Israel stoned him to death, and the king fled in his chariot to Jerusalem. So Israel rebelled against the house of David to this day, and only Judah followed the house of David (1 Kings 12:16-20). Rehoboam gathered a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men to bring the kingdom back, but the word came through Shemaiah not to fight their brethren, for this thing was from the Lord, and they listened and went home (1 Kings 12:21-24).

In his fifth year, because they had transgressed, Shishak king of Egypt came up with a great host and took the fenced cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 12:2-4). Shemaiah told them that because they had forsaken the Lord, He had left them in Shishak’s hand. The princes and the king humbled themselves and said the Lord is righteous (2 Chronicles 12:5-6). When correction comes, the right response is to confess that the Most High is righteous in what He does. Because they humbled themselves He would not destroy them, but they would be Shishak’s servants, to learn the difference between His service and the service of the kingdoms of the countries (2 Chronicles 12:7-8). If Israel confesses its iniquity and accepts the punishment, He remembers His covenant (Leviticus 26:40-42). The people today must likewise humble themselves and accept their condition as righteous judgment.

Shishak carried off the treasures of the Lord’s house and the king’s house and all the shields of gold Solomon had made, and Rehoboam made shields of brass in their place, a fall from gold to brass (2 Chronicles 12:9-10). Because he humbled himself, the wrath turned from him, and in Judah things went well (2 Chronicles 12:12). There was war with Jeroboam all his days, and after seventeen years Abijah his son reigned in his place (2 Chronicles 12:13-16).

Civil authorities who are oppressive do not understand justice.

Warnings of the iniquity of turning from God.

text.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.
And it came to pass, when Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who was yet in Egypt, heard of it, (for he was fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam dwelt in Egypt;)
That they sent and called him. And Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came, and spake unto Rehoboam, saying,
Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.
And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?
And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.
But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him:
And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam the third day, as the king had appointed, saying, Come to me again the third day.
And the king answered the people roughly, and forsook the old men’s counsel that they gave him;

And spake to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke: my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
Wherefore the king hearkened not unto the people; for the cause was from the Lord, that he might perform his saying, which the Lord spake by Ahijah the Shilonite unto Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.
But as for the children of Israel which dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.
And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of the Lord, and all Israel with him.
And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,
With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people were without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
And he took the fenced cities which pertained to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.

Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord is righteous.

And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.
And when the king entered into the house of the Lord, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the Lord turned from him, that he would not destroy him altogether: and also in Judah things went well.

And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.
And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.
Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
The fear of the Lord goeth before the obtaining of authority: but roughness and pride is the losing thereof.
Then king Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute; and all Israel stoned him with stones, that he died. Therefore king Rehoboam made speed to get him up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day.

And it came to pass, when all Israel heard that Jeroboam was come again, that they sent and called him unto the congregation, and made him king over all Israel: there was none that followed the house of David, but the tribe of Judah only.

And when Rehoboam was come to Jerusalem, he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men, which were warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon.
But the word of God came unto Shemaiah the man of God, saying,
Speak unto Rehoboam, the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and unto all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the remnant of the people, saying,

Thus saith the Lord, Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Israel: return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of the Lord, and returned to depart, according to the word of the Lord.
And it came to pass, that in the fifth year of king Rehoboam Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had transgressed against the Lord,
With twelve hundred chariots, and threescore thousand horsemen: and the people were without number that came with him out of Egypt; the Lubims, the Sukkiims, and the Ethiopians.
And he took the fenced cities which pertained to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.

Then came Shemaiah the prophet to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, that were gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and said unto them, Thus saith the Lord, Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak.
Whereupon the princes of Israel and the king humbled themselves; and they said, The Lord is righteous.

And when the Lord saw that they humbled themselves, the word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, saying, They have humbled themselves; therefore I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance; and my wrath shall not be poured out upon Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, and took away the treasures of the house of the Lord, and the treasures of the king’s house; he took all: he carried away also the shields of gold which Solomon had made.
Instead of which king Rehoboam made shields of brass, and committed them to the hands of the chief of the guard, that kept the entrance of the king’s house.
And when the king entered into the house of the Lord, the guard came and fetched them, and brought them again into the guard chamber.
And when he humbled himself, the wrath of the Lord turned from him, that he would not destroy him altogether: and also in Judah things went well.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, are they not written in the book of Shemaiah the prophet, and of Iddo the seer concerning genealogies? And there were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
And Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David: and Abijah his son reigned in his stead.

reuben.name: Reuben
reuben.charge: Lying with Bilhah, his father’s concubine
reuben.summary: Jacob’s firstborn went up to his father’s bed and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it. Paul calls that a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, and the law had already forbidden it, because a father’s wife is the father’s own nakedness. Nothing more is said until the deathbed, where it cost Reuben the birthright: unstable as water, he would not excel.
offenseFull: While Israel dwelt in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it (Genesis 35:22). Paul names the same offense among the Corinthians and calls it a fornication not so much as named among the Gentiles, that a man should have his father’s wife (1 Corinthians 5:1). The law had already forbidden it: the nakedness of a father’s wife is the father’s own nakedness, and the wicked mind that reasons she is not the biological mother is answered before it opens its mouth (Leviticus 18:8). The chapter sets it in the middle of a household being cleaned up. Before going up to Bethel, Jacob had told his house to put away the strange gods among them and be clean, and the terror of God was on the cities round about so that they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob (Genesis 35:2-5). Sin entering the household is the running warning of the chapter. The brief report on Reuben is not an acquittal by silence.
judgmentFull: Jacob called him his firstborn, his might and the beginning of his strength, the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power; then, unstable as water, he would not excel, because he went up to his father’s bed and defiled it (Genesis 49:3-4). The firstborn is the father’s posterity, and dignity and power belonged to him. The chronicle states the transfer plainly: because he defiled his father’s bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright; Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the chief ruler (1 Chronicles 5:1-2). The firstborn lost the place of the heir, as Esau came out first and did not keep it.

Reuben remained a son and a tribe of Israel, and one good line runs through his record. At the pit he delivered Joseph out of his brothers’ hands, telling them to shed no blood, because he meant to bring him back to his father (Genesis 37:21-22); years later, in Egypt, he offered his own two sons as surety for Benjamin (Genesis 42:37). The tribe itself went a-whoring after the gods of the people of the land, the very thing the fringes were given to prevent, so that Israel would look on them and remember the commandments and not go after their own eyes; therefore the Most High stirred up the spirit of Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity, where they remain to this day (1 Chronicles 5:25-26; Numbers 15:39). The blessings of Jacob tell who the tribes are in the last days. Reuben is the so-called Seminole Indian today: great warriors carrying the excellency of power, and unstable as water, nomads always moving, exactly as the scripture said.

text.text: And it came to pass, when Israel dwelt in that land, that Reuben went and lay with Bilhah his father’s concubine: and Israel heard it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve:
It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father’s wife.
The nakedness of thy father’s wife shalt thou not uncover: it is thy father’s nakedness.
Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments:
And let us arise, and go up to Beth–el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
And they gave unto Jacob all the strange gods which were in their hand, and all their earrings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.
And they journeyed: and the terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.
Reuben, thou art my firstborn, my might, and the beginning of my strength, the excellency of dignity, and the excellency of power:
Unstable as water, thou shalt not excel; because thou wentest up to thy father’s bed; then defiledst thou it: he went up to my couch.

Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.
For Judah prevailed above his brethren, and of him came the chief ruler; but the birthright was Joseph’s:)
And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.
And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might rid him out of their hands, to deliver him to his father again.
And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.
And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.

And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and the spirit of Tilgath–pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, and brought them unto Halah, and Habor, and Hara, and to the river Gozan, unto this day.

And it shall be unto you for a fringe, that ye may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them; and that ye seek not after your own heart and your own eyes, after which ye use to go a whoring:

ruth-and-boaz.name: Ruth and Boaz
ruth-and-boaz.charge: Ruth: cleaving to Naomi and joining herself under Israel and Israel’s God. Boaz: the law of the land conducted at the gate before witnesses, and love thy neighbour as thyself
ruth-and-boaz.summary: In the days when the judges ruled, a Moabite widow would not go back to her people and to Chemosh, but bound herself to Naomi’s road, Naomi’s people and Naomi’s God. She came to Bethlehem with a mother in law who called herself Mara, gleaned in the field of Boaz, and called herself what she was to Israel, a stranger. Boaz went up to the gate, called ten elders as witnesses, carried out the law of inheritance and the law of the husband’s brother, and bought the field and Ruth with it, to keep the dead man’s name alive. Their son was Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David.
offenseFull: When the judges ruled, famine drove Elimelech of Bethlehem-judah to Moab with Naomi and their two sons, who married the Moabite women Orpah and Ruth and died there (Ruth 1:1-9). Were the sons of Israel supposed to marry the women of Moab? No. A Moabite was not to enter the congregation of the Lord (Deuteronomy 23:3), and Israel had already gone whoring with the daughters of Moab at Shittim (Numbers 25:1-2); but this was the era of no king, when every man did what was right in his own eyes (Judges 21:25), and even in Ezra’s day the Moabites had not been put away (1 Esdras 8:69). Naomi prayed that each daughter in law find rest in a husband’s house. That rest is an inheritance; a good man leaves one to his children’s children, not a gang of bills (Proverbs 13:22). Behind her words stands the law of the husband’s brother, the widow’s firstborn carrying on the dead man’s name (Deuteronomy 25:5-10). We are not under that
law now, having no land inheritance in this captivity, and it is wicked to pull that scripture today to get with a brother’s widow; but we are still to build a legacy and pass it down.

Orpah went back to her people and her gods, to Chemosh (Numbers 21:29), for all the gods of the nations are idols (Psalms 96:5). Ruth clung to Naomi, her people and her God until death (Ruth 1:14-22). Does that make her an Israelite, or an heir of the kingdom? No. Both daughters in law knew exactly what they were, and Ruth never claimed otherwise. She joined herself under Israel and acknowledged her place, like the woman of Canaan who accepted the crumbs from the masters’ table (Matthew 15:24-28), and like Rahab, who knew the God of Israel was the true living God (Joshua 6:25). Naomi came home to Bethlehem calling herself Mara, bitter.

Ruth gleaned in the field of Boaz, a wealthy kinsman of Elimelech, who kept her with his young women and charged his men not to touch her (Ruth 2:1-16). She asked why he took notice of her, since she was a stranger, the word the law uses for the nations round about (Leviticus 25:44-46). Boaz had heard how she left her own parents and land for her mother in law, prayed that the Lord under whose wings she had taken refuge would reward her, and had handfuls dropped on purpose for her. Naomi then sought that same rest for her, sending her to lie at Boaz’s feet on the threshing floor (Ruth 3:1-18), where Ruth asked him to spread his skirt over her as near kinsman. The skirt is male clothing, the edge of the garment; she was asking the near kinsman to take her under his covering. He blessed her for not going after young men: even as a Moabitess she was keeping the customs of Israel, seeking her dead husband’s kinsman to keep his name in the earth.
judgmentFull: Boaz sat at the gate with the nearer kinsman and ten elders as witnesses, for the record (Ruth 4:1-12). The kinsman had first right to redeem Elimelech’s land, under the law that no inheritance pass from tribe to tribe (Numbers 36:5-9); a man could marry outside his own tribe but not outside the nation. But whoever took the land took the dead man’s wife with it, to keep his name on his inheritance, the duty of the husband’s brother and the loosed shoe. The kinsman declined and drew off his shoe, and Boaz bought all that was Elimelech’s and took Ruth, Mahlon’s widow, as his wife. What law was Boaz exercising in all of that? Loving his neighbour as himself (Leviticus 19:18). That is why he is mentioned in the scriptures.

The elders blessed the marriage, naming Rachel and Leah who built the house of Israel and Pharez whom Tamar bore to Judah; in that blessing they were prophesying of David to come. Ruth bore a son, and Naomi took the child to her bosom and became his nurse (Ruth 4:13-22). Why? Because it is not the custom of Israel to allow a child to be raised under the hand of a heathen. A child’s first teacher is the mother; he takes on her ways, which is what Nehemiah found among the children of the wives of Ashdod, Ammon and Moab, who could not speak the Jews’ language (Nehemiah 13:23-24). Ruth was brought in to keep Mahlon’s name alive in Israel, and she had no hand in raising the child; Naomi raised him so he would learn the ways of Israel. His name was Obed, the father of Jesse, the father of David, the line of Judah running down to the king and on to Christ (Matthew 1:5-6).
