text.text: It came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance.
And David said unto him, From whence comest thou? And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.

And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me. And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him.
And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I.
And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite.
He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me.

So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
And the battle went sore against Saul, and the archers hit him; and he was sore wounded of the archers.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.
And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son; and she bare to Eliphaz Amalek: these were the sons of Adah Esau’s wife.
And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.
And David said unto the young man that told him, Whence art thou? And he answered, I am the son of a stranger, an Amalekite.
And David said unto him, How wast thou not afraid to stretch forth thine hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?
And David called one of the young men, and said, Go near, and fall upon him. And he smote him that he died.
And David said unto him, Thy blood be upon thy head; for thy mouth hath testified against thee, saying, I have slain the Lord’s anointed.
How he met thee by the way, and smote the hindmost of thee, even all that were feeble behind thee, when thou wast faint and weary; and he feared not God.
Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end:

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever:
The Lord forbid that I should stretch forth mine hand against the Lord’s anointed: but, I pray thee, take thou now the spear that is at his bolster, and the cruse of water, and let us go.
He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.
When one told me, saying, Behold, Saul is dead, thinking to have brought good tidings, I took hold of him, and slew him in Ziklag, who thought that I would have given him a reward for his tidings:
And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son:
(Also he bade them teach the children of Judah the use of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.)
Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts.
Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.
Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives, and in their death they were not divided: they were swifter than eagles, they were stronger than lions.

Then said Saul unto his armourbearer, Draw thy sword, and thrust me through therewith; lest these uncircumcised come and thrust me through, and abuse me. But his armourbearer would not; for he was sore afraid. Therefore Saul took a sword, and fell upon it.
And when his armourbearer saw that Saul was dead, he fell likewise upon his sword, and died with him.

the-golden-calf.name: Aaron and Israel at the golden calf
the-golden-calf.charge: Idolatry within weeks of the covenant: the spirit of Egypt still in Israel
the-golden-calf.summary: Not forty days after they heard the voice from the mount, the people told Aaron to make them gods, since they did not know what had become of this Moses. Aaron, who had seen every plague, made the calf and proclaimed a feast to the Lord, and the people feasted and rose up to play. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left. Moses stood in the breach, the sons of Levi drew the sword, and the Lord plagued the people because of the calf that Aaron made.
offenseFull: When the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, they gathered to Aaron and told him to make them gods to go before them, since as for this Moses they did not know what had become of him (Exodus 32:1). Any time deliverance did not come when Israel wanted it, the nation turned, and the leadership got the blame; the same spirit works against the leadership of Israel to this day. Aaron told them to break off the golden earrings in the ears of their wives, their sons and their daughters, which men and women both wore in the scriptures and which is not the sin here; he received the gold, fashioned it with a graving tool and made a molten calf, and they declared it the god that had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, and he built an altar before it and proclaimed a feast to the Lord for the next day (Exodus 32:2-5). Aaron had seen the miracles in Egypt and was set up as high priest, and he still succumbed to the pressure of the people.

The people rose up early, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play; that play was fornication, the same play as at Peor (Exodus 32:6; 1 Corinthians 10:7-8). The Lord told Moses that they had turned aside quickly out of the way he commanded them, and that he had seen this people and it is a stiffnecked people (Exodus 32:8-9). Not forty days gone from the mount, and they had already left his commandments. The spirit that was in Israel in Egypt was still in Israel when they left, and the same holds coming into this truth: the evil carried in from the world will corrupt a man and turn him from the Lord if it is not put off (Ecclesiastes 5:1). They had broken the first two commandments that had just been given at Sinai (Exodus 20:3-5).
judgmentFull: The Lord told Moses to let him alone, that his wrath might wax hot against them and consume them, and he would make of Moses a great nation; Moses was of Levi and of the seed of Jacob, so the Lord could have started over with him (Exodus 32:10). Moses stood in the middle and pleaded the name and the oath: why should the Egyptians say that for mischief he brought them out to slay them in the mountains; and he asked the Lord to remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, to whom he swore by his own self. And the Lord repented of the evil which he thought to do to his people (Exodus 32:11-14). He was never going to break that covenant, for consuming the people would have destroyed the very seed he had sworn to, and his counsel stands from the beginning (Isaiah 46:10).

Joshua heard the noise of the people and said there was a noise of war in the camp, and Moses answered that it was not the voice of them that shout for mastery nor the voice of them that cry for being overcome, but the noise of them that sing (Exodus 32:17-18): they were feasting and dancing around the idol, and Joshua’s loyalty at the mount is one of the main reasons the Lord chose him to follow Moses. When Moses came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, his anger waxed hot; he brake the tables beneath the mount, burnt the calf, ground it to powder, strawed it on the water and made the children of Israel drink of it (Exodus 32:19-20). Aaron answered exactly as Saul would answer afterward, blaming the congregation: they are set on mischief, I cast the gold into the fire, and there came out this calf (Exodus 32:22-24). A leader cannot blame the people he was left in charge of. The people were naked, for Aaron had made them naked to their shame among their enemies, the same nakedness of the

garden, sin uncovered (Exodus 32:25). The sons of Levi answered the call to the Lord’s side, and about three thousand men fell that day, entered separately as their blessing (Exodus 32:26-28). Moses returned to mediate, asking to be blotted out of the Lord’s book if the sin was not forgiven, and the Lord answered that the man who sinned against him is the man he would blot out, and that in the day of his visitation he would visit their sin upon them; and the Lord plagued the people because they made the calf, which Aaron made (Exodus 32:32-35). They changed their glory into the similitude of an ox that eats grass, and forgat God their saviour, which had done great things in Egypt (Psalms 106:19-21).

lawsResolved.text: I am the LORD your God, you shall have no other gods besides me.

text.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.
And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.
And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.
And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the Lord.
And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.
Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.

They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.
Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;
Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.

the-sons-of-samuel.summary: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel in Beersheba, and they did not follow his ways: they chased dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice. The elders of Israel used them as the reason to demand a king like all the nations. No sentence upon the two men is recorded anywhere in the chapter; the sentence that is recorded fell on the nation that used them as an excuse.
offenseFull: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel, Joel the firstborn and Abiah the second, judging in Beersheba. But his sons did not follow his ways: they chased dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice (1 Samuel 8:1-3). The law for the judges in the gates was plain. They were to judge the people justly, not twist judgment, not show partiality, and take no gift, because a bribe blinds even the wise and corrupts the cause of the righteous (Deuteronomy 16:18-20; Exodus 23:8). That gift is what goes into the pocket of a judge and comes back out as a perverted sentence against the man who could not pay.

We see that same thing going on now in this political climate, and even in the church system. It is why the churches will not teach us who we are or teach the commandments of the Most High, and why, when riots and unrest break out, it is those same pastors who are sent out to calm the people down. The contrast with their father was public and undeniable. Samuel could stand before all Israel and ask whose ox or donkey he had taken, whom he had cheated, and from whom he had taken a bribe, and the whole congregation answered that he had taken nothing from anyone (1 Samuel 12:3-4). The sons made the seat of judgment serve their own increase.
judgmentFull: Then all the elders of Israel came to Samuel at Ramah, saying he was old and his sons did not follow his ways, and asking him to appoint a king to judge them like all the nations (1 Samuel 8:4-5). Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a ruler like the other nations have. The corruption was real and the complaint was real; the remedy the people insisted on is its own case, entered next, because the Lord told Samuel that they had not rejected him but had rejected the Lord as their king (1 Samuel 8:7).

No penalty upon Joel or Abiah is recorded. Their own end is not written, and the silence does not turn bribery into righteousness. If a man sees the poor oppressed and justice violently perverted in a province, he is not to be astonished, for a higher official watches over the high one, and One higher still is over them both (Ecclesiastes 5:8). What the record does show is the damage: an office handed down without the character the office requires, a nation that had been delivered by judges for four hundred years handed its excuse, and a demand made at Ramah that cost Israel far more than two corrupt men in Beersheba ever took in bribes.

the-two-women-before-solomon.name: The two women before Solomon
the-two-women-before-solomon.charge: Two harlots, one living child, and a claim that only a sword could sort out
the-two-women-before-solomon.summary: Two harlots who lived in one house each bore a son three days apart; one woman’s child died in the night because she lay on it, and she exchanged it for the living child while the other slept (1 Kings 3:16-22). There was no witness, and before the king each claimed the living child. Solomon called for a sword and ordered the child divided; the true mother gave up her claim to save the child’s life, the other would have it cut in two, and the king gave the child to its mother, so that all Israel saw the wisdom of God in him to do judgment (1 Kings 3:23-28).
offenseFull: The case came before the throne soon after Gibeon, when Solomon had asked for an understanding heart to judge the people and to discern between good and bad (1 Kings 3:9). Two women who were harlots stood before the king. The first said that she and the other woman lived in one house, that she gave birth there, and that three days later the other woman gave birth as well, with no one else in the house but the two of them. The other woman’s child died in the night because she lay on it. She rose at midnight, took the living son from beside the first woman while she slept, laid him in her own bosom, and laid her dead child in the first woman’s bosom. In the morning the first woman rose to nurse her child and found him dead, but when she looked closely in the light she knew it was not the son she had borne (1 Kings 3:16-21). The teaching notes that a child dying under its sleeping mother is something that happens, and it hurts the mothers greatly; and that to an untrained eye one small baby can look like another, but a mother knows her own.

The other woman answered that the living child was hers and the dead one belonged to the first, and the first said the opposite, and so they argued before the king (1 Kings 3:22). How was Solomon to know who was lying and who was telling the truth? He was king over all Israel and did not know these women. There was no stranger in the house to bear witness, both women claimed the same right, and both laid the dead child on the other. The classes add that during the time of Solomon, the Kingdom of Heaven on earth, there were still harlots, and they came to the king in a pair: all flesh keeps company with its own kind.
judgmentFull: The king repeated both claims back to them, called for a sword, and when it was brought he ordered the living child divided in two and half given to each (1 Kings 3:23-25). Then the woman whose child it was spoke, because her heart yearned over her son. She begged the king to give the other woman the living child and by no means kill it. The other said to let it be neither hers nor her rival’s, but divided (1 Kings 3:26). The teaching reads the second woman plainly: she did not care whether the baby was put to death, because she had already lost her own; she wanted company in her misery. It compares her spirit to that of women today who have abortion after abortion and have no love for the child. The king answered that the living child was to be given to the first woman and by no means killed, for she was its mother (1 Kings 3:27).

The Jurisprudence class asks what law Solomon had to go on, since no statute covers one woman taking another’s baby, and answers that he went on the strength of common sense. From the moment he called for the sword he knew the real mother would react in a way the false one would not; he judged by what he had seen of a mother’s love for her child. Wisdom knows things of old and can conjecture aright what is to come; she knows the subtleties of speeches (Wisdom of Solomon 8:8). Conjecture is a conclusion formed on incomplete information, and Solomon had only each woman’s version of the story; by wisdom, experience and the law he reached a right conclusion and recognised the subtlety in the false woman’s speech. Most in the congregation will never be judges, the class says, but they still have to understand judgment, and study is how that wisdom is gained.

All Israel heard of the judgment the king had judged, and they feared the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to do judgment (1 Kings 3:28). This was the answer to what he had asked at Gibeon, made visible to the whole nation through a household dispute between two women. The Lesser and the Greater class then turns to Christ, the greater Solomon, who did not need anyone to testify of man, for he knew what was in man (John 2:24-25). Solomon had to hear the women out and watch their countenance; Christ perceives the thoughts of men before they speak (Luke 5:22). The record gives no separate punishment for the false claimant. It ends with the living child given to his mother.

uzziah.name: Uzziah
uzziah.charge: Going into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense, which appertaineth not unto the king but to the priests the sons of Aaron; and raging at the priests who withstood him
uzziah.summary: Uzziah was made king at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years; as long as he sought God in the days of Zechariah, God made him prosper, against the Philistines, Arabians and Mehunims, in towers, wells, husbandry and a great army with engines of war (2 Chronicles 26:1-15). When he was strong his heart was lifted up, and he went into the temple to burn incense, which belonged only to the priests (2 Chronicles 26:16). When Azariah and eighty priests withstood him he raged with the censer in his hand, and leprosy broke out on his forehead; he lived as a leper, cut off from the house of the Lord, until he died (2 Chronicles 26:17-21).
offenseFull: All the people of Judah made Uzziah king at sixteen in place of Amaziah, and he did right and sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God; as long as he sought the Lord, God made him prosper (2 Chronicles 26:1-5). This Zechariah was a different man from the priest Joash killed. Uzziah is like Joash, who did well while he had the guidance of Jehoiada. All the wise kings consulted with spiritual men; David consulted with every leader (1 Chronicles 13:1), and by wise counsel you make your war (Proverbs 24:5-6). Prosperity comes from the Most High, and it lasts only as long as a man keeps seeking Him.

He broke down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod and built cities among the Philistines, God helped him against the Philistines, the Arabians and the Mehunims, the Ammonites paid gifts, and his name spread to the entrance of Egypt (2 Chronicles 26:6-8). Jehoram had lost Edom and Elath; Uzziah restored Elath to Judah (2 Chronicles 26:2). He built towers, dug wells for his cattle and loved husbandry, a picture of the blessings of Deuteronomy 28 as the Lord made the land fruitful. His army numbered three hundred and seven thousand five hundred, with shields, spears, helmets and slings, and engines invented by cunning men to shoot arrows and great stones; his fame spread far, for the Lord helped him wonderfully until he became strong (2 Chronicles 26:9-15). Together with Jeroboam II in the north, the two kingdoms held borders close to those of David and Solomon; the Lord was giving His people another chance before He began to unleash judgments.

But when he was strong his heart was lifted up to his destruction, and he went into the temple to burn incense on the altar of incense (2 Chronicles 26:16). He got big-headed, a Judahite acting like a Levite. The king was to write a copy of the law and read it all the days of his life, so that his heart would not be lifted up above his brothers (Deuteronomy 17:18-20); the greater you are, the more you should humble yourself (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). Only the seed of Aaron could offer incense, lest a man end like Korah (Numbers 16:40), and the stranger who came near the priest’s office was to die (Numbers 18:7). Azariah the priest and eighty valiant priests withstood him and told him it did not belong to him, to leave the sanctuary, for he had trespassed and it would not be for his honour. Then Uzziah was angry, with a censer in his hand (2 Chronicles 26:17-19). He had beaten nations and would not be corrected by men he counted lower than himself, and he was ready to set fire to the priests of God.
judgmentFull: While he was angry with the priests, the leprosy rose up in his forehead before them beside the incense altar. The priests saw it and thrust him out, and he hurried out himself, because the Lord had struck him (2 Chronicles 26:19-20). He that is soon angry deals foolishly (Proverbs 14:17); one act out of a quick temper cost him a lifetime. The fear of the Lord goes before the obtaining of authority, but roughness and pride is the losing of it, and the Lord brings strange calamities on the proud (Ecclesiasticus 10:13, 21).

He was a leper to the day of his death and lived in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Lord, and Jotham his son was over the king’s house, judging the people (2 Chronicles 26:21). The law said the leper must dwell alone outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46); he was still king in name but could no longer sit on the throne, and leprosy is not merely white skin but a slow deterioration of the whole body. The Lord puts down the mighty from their seats (Luke 1:52). Isaiah wrote the rest of his acts, and they buried him in the field of burial belonging to the kings, not in their sepulchres, because they said he was a leper (2 Chronicles 26:22-23). Stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. In the year king Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up (Isaiah 6:1).

Sixteen years old was Uzziah when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
And he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord, according to all that his father Amaziah did.
And he sought God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God: and as long as he sought the Lord, God made him to prosper.
And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and brake down the wall of Gath, and the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod, and built cities about Ashdod, and among the Philistines.
And God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians that dwelt in Gur–baal, and the Mehunims.
And the Ammonites gave gifts to Uzziah: and his name spread abroad even to the entering in of Egypt; for he strengthened himself exceedingly.
Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, and at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.

Also he built towers in the desert, and digged many wells: for he had much cattle, both in the low country, and in the plains: husbandmen also, and vine dressers in the mountains, and in Carmel: for he loved husbandry.

Moreover Uzziah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands, according to the number of their account by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the ruler, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains.

zacchaeus.name: Zacchaeus
zacchaeus.charge: Extortion as chief of the publicans
zacchaeus.summary: Zacchaeus, chief among the publicans at Jericho and rich, could not see Christ for the crowd, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree, and was called down by name and received him joyfully while the people murmured (Luke 19:1-7). Standing before him he said he gave half of his goods to the poor, and that if he had taken anything from any man by false accusation he restored it fourfold, which is the rate the law names (Luke 19:8; Exodus 22:1). Salvation came to his house, and he was named a son of Abraham, since the Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost (Luke 19:9-10).
offenseFull: Jesus entered and passed through Jericho, and a man named Zacchaeus, who was chief among the publicans and rich, sought to see who he was and could not for the press, because he was little of stature; so he ran before and climbed up into a sycamore tree on the road he would take (Luke 19:1-4). He had been hearing the reports. A cleansed leper had published the matter and blazed it abroad until Christ could no more openly enter a city (Mark 1:40-45), and this man wanted to see for himself who everybody was talking about. The office and the money are the setting of the case; the interest that put him up that tree was already faith.

Christ came to the place, looked up, called him by his name and told him to make haste and come down, for he must abide at his house that day; he made haste and came down and received him joyfully, while the onlookers murmured that he had gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner (Luke 19:5-7). Receiving a man carries a promise with it: he that receives a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward, and even a cup of cold water given in the name of a disciple does not lose its reward (Matthew 10:40-42). That cold water is good news from a far country to a thirsty soul (Proverbs 25:25). The murmurers had already been answered once: the whole need no physician, but they that are sick, and they were sent to go and learn what it means that God will have mercy and not sacrifice (Matthew 9:11-13; Hosea 6:6).
judgmentFull: Zacchaeus stood and said that half of his goods he gave to the poor, and that if he had taken anything from any man by false accusation he restored him fourfold (Luke 19:8). That is a man applying the law to himself. Fourfold is the rate the statute names for a stolen sheep, where an ox requires five (Exodus 22:1); the law of the trespass requires the principal restored with a fifth part added, paid to the man who was wronged (Leviticus 6:1-5; Numbers 5:6-7); and David passed the same fourfold sentence on himself when Nathan set the parable before him (2 Samuel 12:5-6). John had already told publicans coming to his baptism to exact no more than was appointed them, and to bring forth fruits worthy of repentance (Luke 3:8; Luke 3:12-13). A sacrifice cannot stand in the place of dealing justly with the man a person has robbed.

Salvation came to that house that day, and he was called a son of Abraham, because the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost (Luke 19:9-10). Sonship there is by faith, not by the sacrifice: Abraham believed God and it was counted to him for righteousness, and circumcision was afterward the seal of a righteousness of faith he already had (Romans 4:1-3; Romans 4:11). A rich young ruler heard a like word about selling and giving to the poor and went away sorrowful because he had great possessions (Matthew 19:16-22); a rich man hardly enters the kingdom, and yet this rich man did, because his hand was already open. And the salvation spoken over the house is the one Zacharias named, to be saved from our enemies and from the hand of all that hate us (Luke 1:68-74), for the lost that the Son of man came after are the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matthew 15:24).

lawsResolved.text: Stolen livestock which is slaughtered is to be repaid four or five times.
Whoever kills another's animal shall make it good, animal for animal.
If a thief is unable to make restitution for his theft, then he shall be put in servitude to pay what he owes with his labor.

In civil trespasses involving property deceitfully obtained, the person guilty shall confess his crime and make restitution in full for his wrong, and add to it one-fifth of it, and give it to him whom he has wronged.
True repentance is evidenced by one's fruits.

text.text: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;
And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.
And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.
He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward.
And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
As cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?
But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
And Zaccheus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.
And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,

If a soul sin, and commit a trespass against the Lord, and lie unto his neighbour in that which was delivered him to keep, or in fellowship, or in a thing taken away by violence, or hath deceived his neighbour;
Or have found that which was lost, and lieth concerning it, and sweareth falsely; in any of all these that a man doeth, sinning therein:

Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that which was delivered him to keep, or the lost thing which he found,

Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering.
Speak unto the children of Israel, When a man or woman shall commit any sin that men commit, to do a trespass against the Lord, and that person be guilty;

Then they shall confess their sin which they have done: and he shall recompense his trespass with the principal thereof, and add unto it the fifth part thereof, and give it unto him against whom he hath trespassed.
And David’s anger was greatly kindled against the man; and he said to Nathan, As the Lord liveth, the man that hath done this thing shall surely die:
And he shall restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity.

Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father: for I say unto you, That God is able of these stones to raise up children unto Abraham.
Then came also publicans to be baptized, and said unto him, Master, what shall we do?
And he said unto them, Exact no more than that which is appointed you.
And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
What shall we say then that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found?
For if Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory; but not before God.
For what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.

And he received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of the faith which he had yet being uncircumcised: that he might be the father of all them that believe, though they be not circumcised; that righteousness might be imputed unto them also:
And, behold, one came and said unto him, Good Master, what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life?
And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God: but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.
He saith unto him, Which? Jesus said, Thou shalt do no murder, Thou shalt not commit adultery, Thou shalt not steal, Thou shalt not bear false witness,
Honour thy father and thy mother: and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
The young man saith unto him, All these things have I kept from my youth up: what lack I yet?
Jesus said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
But when the young man heard that saying, he went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people,
And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David;
As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us;
To perform the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant;
The oath which he sware to our father Abraham,
That he would grant unto us, that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear,
But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
